SR5.AccessoryCapBall_GE: In combat, each click on Insert rounds spends one Complex Action; the round goes in on the third. Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3.
SR5.AccessoryFlamethrower_GE:
Fire damage, Suppressive Fire allowed (20 units, SR5 p. 179). Fanning mode: Complex Action, up to three targets in range, each within 4 m of another, 2 units.

Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3.
SR5.AccessoryOsmium_GE:
STR 4 or less: Accuracy 3 and DV (STR+2)P. STR 7 or more: Accuracy 5 and DV (STR+6)P. In between, the listed profile.

The Complete Trog p. 177.
SR5.AccessoryVintage_GE: The weapon can never go wireless; its accessories and modifications cost twice the listed amount. Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3.
SR5.ActionSourceReplaceClip: Remove and Insert clip / belt / drum
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopBannerFolder_D: Folder of the vendor banners (3:1 images named after the templates, "Armurier-des-ombres-1.webp"…). Empty: the Megapack ones when it is active, else no banner.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopConfig_D: The item compendiums the shop sells, and who may buy.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationLevel_D: Highest Availability and rating of gear bought in Creation mode (SR5 p. 66 and p. 420). "Custom" uses the two values below.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMaxAvailability: Only used when the creation level is "Custom".
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMaxRating_D: Rating or Device Rating. Only used when the creation level is "Custom"; 0 = no limit.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopGradeGamma_D: Optional rule. Offers gammaware at the counter (Essence ×0.4, Availability +12, cost ×5), never in creation mode.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopGradeGreyware_D: Offers greyware for cyberware only (Essence ×0.75, cost ×1.3), creation included. No wireless. An Awakened character also loses 1 point of Magic (taken automatically) and 1 point of maximum Magic per implant: the shop asks for confirmation before the purchase.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMarketOpen_D: Unticked, players only buy from the GM's vendors (a Grunt carrying a "Shop" storage).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMarketOpen_T: Shop: the market is open to players
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopVendorTest_D: By default an item on the shelf has already been found and is bought without a test (SR5 p. 420: the test is the search). Ticked, the test and the dot come back on the stock.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopVendorTest_T: Shop: availability test at a vendor's too
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritDrainAttribute_D: The book has critters and spirits resist the Drain of an innate spell "with either Intuition or Charisma", at the gamemaster's discretion (SR5 p. 403). The system adds the chosen attribute to Willpower, as a magician's tradition attribute is (Shadow Spells p. 19): a reading, the book does not name Willpower. Spirit sheets only. Charisma by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritDrainAttribute_T: Spirits: attribute resisting the Drain of an innate spell
SR5.SharedVisionShareHint: The checked players see on the map what this device sees, on top of what their own tokens see. Invite Mark is a simple action (SR5 p. 241), counted in combat.
SR5.SharedVisionNoPlayer: No player to share the vision with.
SR5.SharedVisionNoMark: No mark left on {name}: no traffic to intercept (Snoop, SR5 p. 241).
SR5.SharedVisionNoToken: {name} has no token on an active scene: nothing to see through.
SR5.SharedVisionNoPlayerFor: No player owns {name}: nobody to give the vision to.
SR5.AmmunitionTypeLinkHint: Drag an Ammunition Type item here to link it
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopContactFence_D: Percentage of the listed price a contact pays per point of Loyalty (SR5 p. 421: 5).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopContactFence_T: Fence: share paid by a contact
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMode_D: Add gear from the shop without charging it. World setting, gamemaster only.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDealerKeywords_D: Comma-separated words. A contact whose type contains one of them gets the +2 Bargaining specialization on availability tests.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDealerKeywords_T: Shop: contact types that deal in goods
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBase_D: What a found buyer starts from, as a percentage of the listed price (SR5 p. 421: 25).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBase_T: Fence: share of the listed price
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBuyerPool_D: Dice the buyer haggles with. The book gives none, so the table sets it.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceStep_D: How much each net hit of the haggling moves the price, either way (SR5 p. 421: 5).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceThreshold_D: Threshold of the extended Etiquette + Charisma test (SR5 p. 421: 10).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceThreshold_T: Fence: threshold to find a buyer
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMaxSurchargeDice_D: Most dice a surcharge can buy (SR5 p. 420: 12, four times the price). 0 removes the cap.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopSurchargePerDie_D: Percentage of the price to offer on top for one extra die on the availability test (SR5 p. 420: 25).
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_flag: Actors whose "Can shop" box is ticked
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_folder: Actors in the folder below (sub-folders included)
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_folderOrFlag: The folder or the "Can shop" box
SR5.ShopCartBlocked: A cart line will not go through the till: hover it to see why.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDelivery_D: An item with an availability is found after the search time (SR5 p. 420): it is paid when ordered, waits on the sheet under "On order", and the GM delivers it with one click when the world clock reaches its due time. "Immediate" delivers at checkout, as before.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpress_D: Not in the book. The player may tick "Express" when ordering: she pays a surcharge and receives sooner. It is a better deal than the surcharge of the book (SR5 p. 420), on purpose.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpressSurcharge_D: Share of the base price added to a line delivered express.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpressFactor_D: The search time the test gave is divided by this number.
SR5.ShopExpressLabel: Express: +{surcharge}% of the price, time divided by {factor}
SR5.ShopOrderCancelAsked: Cancellation request sent to the GM.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelText: {user} asks to cancel the order of {actor}: {name}. {price} ¥ will be refunded.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelRefused: The GM refused to cancel the order of {actor}: {name}.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelVendor: The vendor {vendor} pays it back: its cashbox first, its accounts for the rest.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelNoVendor: No vendor in the GM's ledger: only the sheet is refunded.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelNotInLedger: Not in the GM's ledger: no automatic refund. Refund by hand if the order is real.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelDebitGone: The debit of this purchase ({paid} ¥) was deleted or lowered on the sheet: {left} ¥ is left, and the refund stops there.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM cancels an order: they keep the order ledger.
SR5.SocketUseConfirm: {user} asks: {what}. The card comes from their player: the system counted {value} again on its dice, within the sheet's pool, but cannot check the dice themselves. Apply?
SR5.WARN_WoundGroupTreated: {user} asks to heal {patient}, but this group of wounds has been treated already (first aid or the Heal spell once per group, no first aid after Heal; core rulebook p. 207-208). Nothing is applied: new damage opens a new group. If that is the case and the system did not see it, heal by hand.
SR5.SocketUseConfirmRead: {user} asks: {what}. The hold ({value}) is read on their player's card: the system does not count it again on the dice and cannot check it. Apply?
SR5.SocketUseMarks: {name} ({marks} mark(s); hits counted again: the winner's)
SR5.SocketUse_grappleEscape: break free from the hold of {target}
SR5.ShopConfigBuyersHint: A player only ever sees the characters they own.
SR5.ShopConfigShelvesHint: Ticked compendiums are sold. Qualities, spells, powers and other non-goods never are. A compendium added later is sold by default.
SR5.ShopCreationModeHint: Gear is added without being charged: character creation, or fixing an item already paid for.
SR5.ShopDealerSpecialization: Dealer: +2 dice for the Bargaining specialization.
SR5.ShopDefaulting: No Negotiation on the contact sheet: defaulting, Charisma - 1 (SR5 p. 55).
SR5.ShopDerivedPool: Contact sheet left empty: pool read off its Connection (Run Faster p. 174).
SR5.ShopEquipModeHint: GM: place any item on any actor, free and without a transaction. Prototypes and every grade are allowed.
SR5.ShopFenceCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: the wrong people are now interested.
SR5.ShopFenceImmediate: Taken on the spot, no questions asked.
SR5.ShopFenceNoBuyer: No buyer found. Try again later, or through a contact.
SR5.ShopFenceTeamworkHint: Rare goods are easier to place: the availability rating is rolled as a teamwork test and its hits join the search pool (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopGradeGone: {name}: this grade is no longer offered here (at creation: used, standard, alphaware). Remove the line and add it again.
SR5.ShopEssenceConfirmText: {name}: this purchase would take Essence down to {essence}. At 0, the character dies (SR5 p. 54). Confirm anyway?
SR5.ShopMarketClosed: The GM closed the market: buy from the vendors. Pick a shop at the top left.
SR5.ShopOddsHint: A landmark, not a probability: green when the pool beats the Availability by 2 or more, orange within 1, red below (Negotiation + Charisma [Social] vs Availability, SR5 p. 420).
SR5.ShopOverrideLimitHint: Limit typed in by hand: replaces the computed one. Leave empty to compute it.
SR5.ShopOverridePoolHint: Dice pool typed in by hand: replaces the computed one for the availability test. Leave empty to compute it.
SR5.ShopPartialPool: Charisma missing from the contact sheet: read off its Connection (Run Faster p. 174).
SR5.ShopPurchaseDescription: Bought from the compendium browser: {name}, for {price}¥.
SR5.ShopRetryHint: Failure: the test may be tried again after twice the search time (SR5 p. 420). The GM checks the wait and rolls the test.
SR5.ShopRetryText: Same searcher, same item. You may change the surcharge offered (% of the price); the GM rolls the test.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_unknown: New test refused for {name}: the GM did not record when this failure happened (card missing from their ledger).
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_used: New test refused for {name}: this failure was already tried again.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_early: New test refused for {name}: wait twice the search time, until {date}.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_notFailed: New test refused for {name}: the GM’s ledger records no failure for this line (a critical glitch gives none).
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorGone: New test refused for {name}: the vendor no longer exists.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorClosed: New test refused for {name}: the vendor’s shop is closed.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorCeiling: New test refused for {name}: its Availability is over the vendor’s ceiling.
SR5.ShopSentToActiveGM: Request passed to the active GM ({name}): their browser keeps the shop's ledger.
SR5.ShopOrderActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM delivers an order: their browser keeps the shop's ledger.
SR5.ShopTestSent: Availability test sent to the GM: they roll the dice and post the card.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorGone: Availability test refused: the vendor no longer exists.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorClosed: Availability test refused: the vendor’s shop is closed.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorCeiling: Availability test refused for {name}: its Availability is over the vendor’s ceiling.
SR5.WARN_ShopTestNoGM: No GM connected: the availability test is rolled by the GM and did not happen. Try again when a GM is here.
SR5.WARN_ShopCardNotByGM: This card was not rolled by the GM: it cannot be cashed. Test the availability again.
SR5.ShopSaleGone: Nothing sold: the goods were no longer there.
SR5.ShopSellOnMarketHint: Extended Etiquette + Charisma [Social] test to find a buyer, then haggling over the price (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopSellToContactHint: The contact takes the goods on the spot, no test, for a share of the listed price per point of Loyalty (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopVendorApproveText: {user} wants to buy for {actor}: {name}, {price}¥. Accept the sale?
SR5.ShopVendorBannerHint: Wide 3:1 image shown at the top of the shop.
SR5.ShopVendorBuyAllHint: Unticked, the vendor only buys what it sells (its shelves).
SR5.ShopVendorChatFree: {actor} receives {name} from {shop}'s stock, free of charge.
SR5.ShopVendorClearConfirm: Delete the {count} item(s) in {name}'s stock? The cashbox is left alone.
SR5.ShopVendorClientsHint: The characters for whom this vendor is a contact, and their Loyalty: only they sell at 5% × Loyalty (SR5 p. 421). Kept here by the GM, never read off the player's sheet.
SR5.ShopVendorContactEmpty: drop a contact on the vendor
SR5.ShopVendorContactHint: The contact who looks for what the vendor does not stock: its Connection gives its pool (Run Faster p. 174). Without one, the vendor's sheet. Dropping a contact on the shop window makes it the searcher.
SR5.ShopVendorLinkedHint: Linked: one stock, however many tokens. Unlinked: each token is a shop of its own.
SR5.ShopVendorMarginHint: Added to the book price (negative for a discounter). The GM adjusts prices to the local market (SR5 p. 419).
SR5.ShopVendorMaxAvailabilityHint: Ceiling of the automatic restock; an item placed by hand may exceed it. 0 = no ceiling.
SR5.ShopVendorNoActor: Put this storage on an NPC (Grunt): it is the one selling.
SR5.ShopVendorNoBanner: No banner of this template in the chosen folder.
SR5.ShopVendorNoBannerFolder: No banner folder: set "Shop: banner folder" in the world settings.
SR5.ShopVendorOfferContact: Contact {name}, Loyalty {loyalty}: {percent}% of the listed price, no test (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: the vendor is insulted, and maybe worse (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferGlitch: Glitch: the vendor is annoyed, the sale may be compromised (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferHaggle: Negotiation: {hits} hits ({pool} dice) against {vendorHits} ({vendorPool} dice): {percent}% of the listed price (SR5 p. 421).
SR5.ShopVendorOnOrderHint: Items of its shelves it does not stock show as "on order": the vendor looks for them with its own Negotiation and Charisma (SR5 p. 420).
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_name: price proposed from the name, on the shelves
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_sheet: price proposed from the character's sheet
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_source: price proposed from the source the item declares
SR5.ShopVendorOverflow: Cashbox full: {amount}¥ went to the vendor's accounts.
SR5.ShopVendorPoolHint: The vendor's Negotiation + Charisma when its sheet is empty (0 = the sheet). Templates give 8: a professional Grunt, a choice of play.
SR5.ShopVendorRestockReading: {name}: reading the shelves for the restock… (up to a minute after a reload)
SR5.ShopVendorRestockBusy: {name}: a restock is already running, wait for it to finish.
SR5.ShopVendorReviewText: {seller} sells for {price}¥. Check each item against its source, then accept, refuse or correct the price.
SR5.ShopVendorSearches: {name} looks for what is not on the shelves (SR5 p. 420).
SR5.ShopVendorSellHint: The GM makes the offer: a contact standing for this vendor takes it at 5% × Loyalty, otherwise an opposed Negotiation test, 25% ± 5% per net hit (SR5 p. 421). The vendor is there: no search for a buyer.
SR5.ShopVendorTemplateHint: The template sets shelves, legality, margin and max availability: choices of play, not rules. Everything stays editable on the storage sheet. The Magic shelf holds foci only, the only magic goods the compendiums sell.
SR5.ShopWindowFailed: The shop could not open: see the console (F12).
SR5.AggravatedWoundBox: Aggravated wound: counts double for healing (right-click to remove the mark)
SR5.WARN_ButtonClaimed: Another owner of this character is already using this button: wait for their card (if nothing comes, try again in a minute).
SR5.WARN_CapBallRoundByRound: Cap & Ball: in combat this weapon reloads round by round (3 Complex Actions per round).
SR5.INFO_CapBallStep: Cap & Ball: reloading {done}/{total}. Stopping before the end means starting over.
SR5.WARN_DroneWirelessOnGMOnly: Only the gamemaster turns a switched-off drone back on: nobody can reach it wirelessly to ask it.
SR5.INFO_AmmoAlreadyFull: The weapon is already full: nothing to reload.
SR5.INFO_SourceModifiersCleaned: SR5 migration done: computed modifiers removed from the stored data (actors: {actors}, world items: {items}, unlinked tokens: {tokens}).
SR5.INFO_SourceModifiersRunning: SR5 migration running: cleaning the computed modifiers stored in the actors. This may take a minute; do not close the world.
SR5.WARN_SourceModifiersDeferred: SR5 migration put off: a combat is under way or has its initiatives rolled. It will run at the next load of the world with no combat and no initiative rolled.
SR5.WARN_SourceModifiersFailed: SR5 migration incomplete: {failed} element(s) could not be cleaned (see the console). It will be taken up again at the next load of the world.
SR5.EffectCardRejected: Effect ignored ({item}, card from {user}): it does not come from the caster's owner, or its dice cannot be read. Apply it by hand if needed.
SR5.UnresistedDamageConfirm: {item} deals {value} box(es) to the {monitor} monitor of {actor}, with no resistance test. Apply?
SR5.WARN_UnresistedDamageNotOwner: You do not own this actor: the GM must apply this damage.
SR5.EffectCardConfirm: {user}: {caster}, {item}. Hits counted again on the dice: {hits}, net hits: {netHits}. Apply the effect with these values?
SR5.ToxinCardConfirm: {user}: {toxin} ({weapon}) on {actor}. Power read again: {power}, hits counted again on the dice: {hits}. Damage: {damage}. Effects: {effects}. Apply?
SR5.ToxinCardRejected: Toxin effect ignored ({user}'s card, on {actor}): the card does not come from the actor's owner, the weapon that carried the toxin cannot be found, or its dice cannot be read. Apply it by hand if needed.
SR5.ToxinCardSpent: Toxin effect already applied ({user}'s card, on {actor}).
SR5.EffectDefinitionTitle: Effect defined on a player’s sheet
SR5.EffectDefinitionIntro: {item}, on {owner}’s sheet, is about to apply to {actor}:
SR5.EffectDefinitionIntroArea: {item}, on {owner}’s sheet, is about to apply to the tokens of its template (the first: {actor}). Your answer stands for the whole template:
SR5.EffectDefinitionNoResistance: No resistance test: the sheet says this spell is not resisted.
SR5.EffectDefinitionNoReference: No reference found (compendium or world item): check the sheet before applying.
SR5.EffectDefinitionRefResisted: The reference calls for a resistance test: cancel to have the target resist.
SR5.EffectDefinitionRefNotResisted: The sheet calls for a resistance test, the reference does not.
SR5.EffectCardMismatch: The card stated {hits} hits and {netHits} net hits.
SR5.EffectCardOverPool: The card shows more dice than the pool worked out again ({allowed}, Edge included): only the first ones count.
SR5.EffectCardItemMismatch: {item}: the caster's sheet holds {written} hits, the dice of his card give {hits}. The template applies {hits}.
SR5.TemplateFlagsIgnored: Template from {user} ({item}): the light, visibility, noise or background count written on it are ignored. Only the ones its item gives count. Place a template yourself if the scene calls for it.
SR5.ThresholdModifierHint: added to the threshold of the test if it has one, no effect on a test without threshold.
SR5.AimForPerfectionReminder: Aim for Perfection: pick a Called Shot, unless laying down cover fire or doing something a Called Shot does not fit (Assassin's Primer p. 15).
SR5.WARN_VintageElectronic: {weapon} is a Vintage weapon: {accessory} will have no wireless effect on it (Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3).
SR5.WARN_VintageNoWireless: A Vintage weapon can never go wireless (Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3).
SR5.RADIATION_SceneHint: Radiation severity of the scene (Run & Gun p. 164-165). Nothing happens without the button: it opens the list of exposed characters.
SR5.RADIATION_Exposed: {actor}: exposed, feels a {level} severity; first test on {time}.
SR5.RADIATION_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the radiation ledger.
SR5.RADIATION_OutcomeStunOne: {actor}: Power {power}, {hits} hits, 1 Stun box and Nausea.
SR5.RADIATION_OutcomeStun: {actor}: Power {power}, {hits} hits, {remaining} Stun boxes and Nausea.
SR5.RADIATION_Reminders: Reminders (Run & Gun p. 165), not automated: after a Severe or worse exposure the character radiates within 10 m himself. No healing test in a radioactive zone. Moderate: unconscious after 72 h, dead 72 h later.
SR5.AntitoxinNeutralized: Neutralized by the antitoxin: no effect
SR5.Anticoagulant_GE: The critter’s attack carries some form of anti-coagulant that keeps the target’s blood from clotting. Once hit with this power, the victim’s blood continues to flow, causing two boxes of Stun damage every minute that cannot be resisted. The bleeding can be stopped with a medkit (or better medical equipment) and a First Aid + Logic [Mental] (3) Test.
SR5.AssensingResult1a: The general state of the subject’s health (healthy, injured, ill, etc.).
SR5.AssensingResult1b: The subject’s general emotional state or impression (happy, sad, angry, etc.).
SR5.AssensingResult1c: Whether the subject is mundane or Awakened.
SR5.AssensingResult2a: The presence and location of cyberware implants.
SR5.AssensingResult2b: The class of a magical subject (fire elemental, manipulation spell, power focus, curse ritual, and so on).
SR5.AssensingResult2c: If you have seen the subject’s aura before, you may recognize it, regardless of physical disguises or alterations
SR5.AssensingResult3a: The presence and location of alphaware cyber implants.
SR5.AssensingResult3b: Whether the subject’s Essence, Magic and Force are higher, lower, or equal to your own.
SR5.AssensingResult3c: A general diagnosis for any maladies (diseases or toxins) the subject suffers.
SR5.AssensingResult3d: Any astral signatures present on the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult4a: The presence and location of bioware implants and betaware cyber implants.
SR5.AssensingResult4b: The exact Essence, Magic, and Force of the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult4c: The general cause of any astral signature (combat spell, alchemical combat spell, air spirit, and so on).
SR5.AssensingResult5a: The presence and location of deltaware implants, gene treatments, and nanotech.
SR5.AssensingResult5b: An accurate diagnosis of any disease or toxins which afflict the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult5c: The fact that a subject is a technomancer.
SR5.AttackModFiringFromVehicle: Attacker firing from a moving vehicle
SR5.AttackModFiringWithImagingDevice: Attacker firing from cover with imaging device
SR5.CompendiumBrowserFailed: The compendium browser could not be opened. See the console for details.
SR5.ChooseItemToPan: Choose item to add to PAN
SR5.ClickForDetails: Click here to display or hide details
SR5.GrappleReversed: Situation reversed: {holder} now holds {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold} (Run & Gun p. 126).
SR5.GrappleClinchTaken: {holder} clinches {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}. {holder} has the superior position; Reach cancelled between them; melee weapons: penalty equal to their Reach, firearms: penalty of {hold}; they only move together, 2 m per action (Run & Gun p. 133).
SR5.HELP_GrappleClinchMsg: Clinch: Agility + Gymnastics [Physical] against Reaction + Intuition (Run & Gun p. 133). Target the opponent. Requires martial arts training.
SR5.GrappleHoldChanged: {holder}'s hold on {held} is now {hold}. To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}.
SR5.GrappleHoldTaken: {holder} subdues {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}. Keeping the hold costs a Complex Action each action phase (SR5 p. 195).
SR5.GrappleNoHold: No hold: Strength and net hits do not exceed the Physical limit
SR5.SETTINGS_GrapplingRules_D: Clinch, subdue, escape and reversal (SR5 p. 195-196, Run & Gun p. 126 and 133-138): linked statuses on the tokens and computed thresholds. Unchecked, nothing changes.
SR5.SETTINGS_RunningFromDistance_D: Running (SR5 p. 163-164): the "Running" status is put on when a token in combat is moved with the "Run" or "Sprint" action. Checked, it is also put on as soon as the token has gone farther than its walking rate this Combat Turn. Unchecked by default: a token moved by hand to tidy the map would count as running.
SR5.SETTINGS_RunningFromDistance_T: Put the "Running" status on from the distance covered
SR5.WARN_GrappleAlreadyHeld: One of the fighters is already in a hold: one hold per token.
SR5.WARN_GrappleHoldChanged: The hold has changed since this roll: this button no longer applies.
SR5.WARN_GrappleNotYourHold: Only the GM and the owner of the one holding can use these buttons.
SR5.WARN_GrappleNeedsMartialArts: The clinch requires martial arts training (Run & Gun p. 133): this character has none. The GM decides.
SR5.CyberEyesReplacedVision: Cybereyes: the vision of the metatype is replaced.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_ActivateDescription: The mentioned {type} is currently installed but has not been activated. To activate it for the current game system, check its box and save your modification in the 'Manage Modules' window of the 'Game Settings' application tab.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_Description1: The installed system has declared dependencies, but not all of the requirements were met.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_Description2: Although the system will run in its current setup, user experience and/or functionnalities might be degraded.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_Description3: For the best possible result with this game system, it is strongly recommended that the following steps be taken as soon as possible.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_GoToSetupScreen: Go to the configuration and setup screen
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_InstallDescription: The mentioned {type} is currently missing. To install it, head over the 'Add-on Modules' tab from the 'Configuration and Setup' screen.
SR5.DEPENDENCIES_UpdateDescription: The mentioned {type} is currently installed but is out of date. To update it, head over the 'Add-on Modules' tab from the 'Configuration and Setup' screen.
SR5.AIProgramsNoDevice: No programs outside a device (Data Trails p. 157)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_NoDevice: The AI was on no device: it resists with Willpower + Depth (Data Trails p. 161).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_OnDevice: The AI ran on a device that is not bricked: it resists with Willpower + Firewall + Depth (Data Trails p. 161).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Bricked: The device {device} is bricked: no Firewall, and its Device Rating ({rating}) is added to the Essence to resist (Data Trails p. 161).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_EdgeEscape: Before resolving: the AI may burn 1 point of Edge to jump to a grid and escape the dissipation; it then loses a random advanced program. If so, do not resolve this card.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Rule: The AI always loses 1 point of Essence, plus 1 per box of overflow damage not resisted. It also loses 1 point of Depth (minimum 1).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Surplus: Overflow damage (boxes beyond the monitor, to check)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_SurplusFromPlayer: This overflow was worked out by a player's client: check it.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_DeviceRatingAdded: + {rating} (rating of the bricked device) to resist
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Extra: Extra dice, or fewer (HELLO WORLD!: +1 per rank, Data Trails p. 153)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Result: {pool} dice, {hits} hits against {toResist} to resist: {loss} point(s) of Essence lost.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Reminders: Left to the GM: remove a random advanced program (never learned again) and give a Fragmentation trait if Essence was lost, once per event (Data Trails p. 161).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Destroyed: Essence at 0: the core is too corrupted to be restored, the AI is destroyed (Data Trails p. 161).

SR5.IceAcid_GE: Acid IC targets and overwrites your protective software. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Firewall by 1. If your Firewall has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.
SR5.IceBinder_GE: Binder IC corrupts your base operating system. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Data Processing by 1. If your Data Processing has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.
SR5.IceBlack_GE: Black IC is the most feared intrusion countermeasures program on the market. The hosts that run it don’t want you repelled—they want you dead. When it hits, Black IC link-locks you. It also causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target) along with an equal amount of biofeedback damage.
SR5.IceBlaster_GE: Also known as Grey IC, a Blaster IC program’s attack causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage, +1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target, with biofeedback damage. The biofeedback from a Blaster program can only cause Stun damage. A single successful attack also link-locks the target.
SR5.IceBlueGoo_GE: If an avatar successfully deals Matrix damage to this IC, it deactivates by exploding. Make a Host Rating x 2 [Attack] v. Logic + Firewall Opposed Test. If this attack hits, the avatar is link-locked by the host that launched the Blue Goo. The avatar must resist (Attack) DV, and it is marked by the host. The avatar must successfully Jack Out of the host to end the link-lock.
SR5.IceCrash_GE: If Crash IC has a mark on you (through its host) and hits, one of your programs crashes, selected at random. Programs crashed this way can’t be run again until after a reboot.
SR5.IceFlicker_GE: Flicker link-locks you when it hits and puts a mark on you. If you have two marks on you, it disconnects you from the Matrix, dealing dumpshock damage if appropriate. Although you have been disconnected from the Matrix, your avatar doesn’t disappear until you log back in using the same device, or after [Device Rating] rounds. It remains where you left it, unable to act, while other IC can attempt to trace your location or analyze your avatar.
SR5.IceJammer_GE: Jammer IC turns your firewall against your own attacks. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Attack by 1. If your Attack has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.
SR5.IceKiller_GE: This IC is a simple but effective cybercombat program that causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark) on the target with each successful attack.
SR5.IceMarker_GE: Marker IC installs tiny worm programs that mess with your datastreams. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Sleaze by 1. If your Sleaze has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.
SR5.IcePatrol_GE: Patrol IC acts more like an agent than other intrusion countermeasures. Its job is to patrol a host, scanning people’s marks and looking for illegal activity using the Matrix Perception action on all targets in the host. While the act of placing a mark is an illegal activity, the act of simply having a mark is not. Once you have the mark, you are considered a legitimate user. Patrol IC has no attack, but it shares its information with its parent host. Since the Patrol IC doesn’t use Attack actions, it doesn’t take Matrix damage when it fails. Most hosts have Patrol IC and keep it running all the time.
SR5.IceProbe_GE: The task of Probe IC is to mark intruders for other IC. Every successful “attack” means another mark for the host and its IC on the target, up to the maximum of three marks.
SR5.IceScramble_GE: Scramble IC nukes your connection to the Matrix and forces you to reboot. If the host has three marks on you when this IC hits you, you reboot immediately, taking dumpshock if you were in VR.
SR5.IceSleuther_GE: This IC puts a mark on you if it hits. Each mark provides a legitimate user with +2 dice on any Matrix Search actions or Matrix Perception tests involving you. It works by applying different behavioral algorithms and heuristics to try to work out what sort of person you are. This IC also installs tracker code into your avatar, enabling the IC to identify which grids and hosts your avatar visits after the mark lands. Marks from this IC may be removed normally
SR5.IceSparky_GE: Sparky IC is also known as “Psycho Killer,” an upgraded version of the popular Killer IC. It causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target) with biofeedback damage.
SR5.IceTarBaby_GE: The Tar Baby IC link-locks you when it hits. If you’re already link-locked, it puts a mark on you, up to a maximum of three marks.
SR5.IceTrack_GE: Track IC follows the datastreams between your icon and your deck. If this IC hits and the host has two marks or more on you, the host (and its owners) discover your physical location, which is usually reported to real-world authorities immediately.

SR5.LifestyleComforts_GE:
Comforts & Necessities are an integral part of any lifestyle. If a shadowrunner doesn’t get a good night’s rest and a belly full of nutrient-added soy, he’ll eventually end up at the morgue. This is because of the possibility of fatigue damage (p. 172, SR5). At the beginning of most game sessions, characters roll to resist fatigue damage, simulating how much rest they have been able to get in their quarters. Characters do not, however, have to make this roll if the new session directly continues an adventure from the previous one and they have not had a chance to rest in whatever domicile is part of their lifestyle. Base Fatigue damage that characters must resist is 6S. For each level in the Comforts & Necessities category, reduce the DV by 2.

Additional factors may affect the damage the character must resist. For example, having allergies can be a hassle, especially food allergies where choices are limited. Allergies to things found in the environment (such as pollution, ultraviolet rays, plastic, etc.) increase the Fatigue damage characters must resist by 1 per level above mild for common allergies and 1 per level above moderate for uncommon allergies if the Comforts & Necessities category of the lifestyle is level three or lower. Allergies to foods can be problematic, as some special dietary requirements may not be available in all lifestyles. Allergies to common foodstuffs (soy, mycoprotein, etc.) also increase the fatigue damage value by 1 per level above mild if the Comforts & Necessities category of the lifestyle is level 3 or lower. For uncommon allergies, the damage value increases by 1 if the allergy is Severe, 2 if it is Extreme.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionAngryDrunkReputation_: You have a bad reputation for causing or being in fights. This has caused many bars to put your picture in their system or ban you completely. The character cannot have any Bar Patron or Patron of the Arts (Private Club) entertainment options attached to any lifestyle, This option may cause issues for the character when meeting Mr. Johnson. Once the character gets away from the neighborhood where they live, though, they leave the bad reputation behind. Add 1 point to the base lifestyle associated with this quality
SR5.LifeStyleOptionArmory_GE: Quite popular among shadowrunners is a room dedicated to guns. Ammo and one stock firearm duplicating one that the character purchased at the character creation are on hand in this room. If the character has purchased a toolkit that can work on the particular weapon, 1 point of Accuracy or AP can be repaired per week without additional cost. A point of Reach can also be repaired in two weeks.

This service can be purchased several times for similar services such as landscape care, beauty salon/barber, and basic car cleaning/maintenance. These services provide a reasonable amount of privacy. These services can also include some specific enhancements. Mage-sensitive services destroy biomaterials of the individual that may be left behind on clothing or in a car/premise. Any material link items found of the character at his domicile or in his vehicle are contaminated and cannot be used for ritual purposes.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionCleaningServicePollut: Cleaning services include tidying up the home and cleaning/mending clothes sent to them with some semblance of privacy guarantee. SR5.LifeStyleOptionCorporateOwned_GE: This domicile is within the jurisdiction of a corporation, such as a wageslave housing complex or arcology. Increase both the Comforts & Necessities value and limit of the location by 1. The Security level and limit are also increased by 1 from the base lifestyle. Reduce the available points of the lifestyle by 3. If the base lifestyle doesn’t have 3 points to start with, then it can’t be corporate owned. To use this quality, characters must have a corporate or limited corporate SIN (p. 84, SR5)
SR5.LifeStyleOptionCramped_GE: Applies to a single asset (Garage or Workshop). Can be purchased once for each asset, reducing its monthly cost by ten percent. Any tests performed in the cramped space have their Limit reduced by 2.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionDangerousArea_GE: Isn’t that where a guy got shot yesterday? The area you live in is particularly dangerous and prone to crime, including violence. Security and law enforcement are overwhelmed in the area, so will only respond to the most desperate need and will often be slower to respond. People in the area generally look out for themselves. Hey, at least your rent is cheaper, just don’t keep any fancy stuff in your place. Any High Threat Response (see p. 356) or other similar security response rolls are made as if this area were one level lower than it actually is.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionDifficultToFind_GE: Cannot have a Discreet Deliveryman or Candyman entertainment options attached to this lifestyle. Add 1 point to the base lifestyle.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionDiscreetCleaningServi: You know of an organization that can go to a premise and patch bullet holes, wash out blood stains, and cleanse the astral in under twenty-four hours (as long as it’s not a public or corporate place). At the listed cost, they will handle only one body disposal a month. If this limit is exceeded, the company may drop the character as a client. This service is tied to the character, so it does not end when they change lifestyles, as long as they keep paying the cost.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionDiscreetDeliveryman_G: You know a guy who can pick up and deliver any legal item (within reason) without being noticed to your domicile. It may be one of many bicycle couriers dashing over New York streets or a street urchin who can avoid many observers—either way, the delivery service is subtle enough to not be noticed by observers. The Discreet Deliveryman/Candyman has a dice pool of 14 for Sneaking Tests and an Edge Rating of 4. They only cover delivering an item—the purchase of the item must be accomplished through normal means. Time to deliver is based on original price of the item. While the deliveryman can handle takeout food service and legal items with an Availability of 8 or less, the candyman can handle items up to Availability of 16, as well as restricted and illegal items.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionExtraSecure_GE: Security where you live is particularly tight. The neighborhood may be surrounded by a wall, guarded by vigilant security contractors, patrolled by an altruistic gang, or near some particularly powerful individual that no one wants to mess with. Whatever the case, the security of the living space is above average for the area. All High Threat Response (see p. 356) and other security response rolls are made at one level better than the area would normally be.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionGarageAirplane_GE: A garage is a large covered area with enough space to park and maintain a single vehicle. With the purchase of a Shop (p. 443, SR5) related to the vehicle, 1 box of damage to the vehicle can be repaired per week without additional financial cost, as the cost is absorbed by the lifestyle. Purchasing a Facility increases the repair rate to 2 boxes of damage. Use the Build and Repair rules for quicker repairs (p.145, SR5, and p. 143, Run & Gun). This asset can be purchased more than once so that multiple vehicles can be serviced at the same time. The points cost, monthly nuyen cost, and minimum lifestyle depend on the nature of the vehicle, as listed in the table.

Commlinks and home entertainment systems connect you wirelessly to everything from photos you’ve taken to corporate-sponsored lines of entertainment that you can watch whenever you want. Having this asset reduces the Comforts & Necessities environmental damage due to pollution allergies by 1 point.

You may get an occasional free drink there from your buddies. Similar habitual locations include restaurants and fast-food joints. One specific location is chosen when this entertainment option is selected, and the feature can be purchased more than once to add different locations.

SR5.LifeStyleOptionMerchandiseGoods_GE: This location will provide some sort of legal goods for sale. The item to be sold must be selected when this option is purchased. The base Availability for the selected item is 3 for gear and low quality for miscellaneous items. For better quality or higher availability, more points must be spent to buy this service, with the maximum being 4 points to sell a luxury-quality item. Each point also adds 2 to the Availability of the item that can be sold on the premises. The character may pick up said item at a ten percent discount and reduce the interval on the Extended Test to locate the item by 1 category (days to hours, and hours to “it’s on the shelf over there”).
SR5.LifeStyleOptionMerchandisePawnShop_G: Any used legal goods can be fenced at this location. Items can be sold within a week provided that the player sells the item at fifteen percent of the normal purchase price.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionMerchandiseUsedGoods_: This location can be used to fence one specific item, which must be selected when this option is purchased. SR5.LifeStyleOptionNotAHome_GE: This location was not designed for habitation. There’s no plumbing and possibly no privacy, lacking standard features such as interior walls. SR5.LifeStyleOptionPublicTransportation_: You have a monthly pass to access public transportation in your region. This can involve taking a bus, trolley, subway, ferry, or any combination of them. This means from most places within the city you have transportation access to your destination, with the caveat that it’s not as fast as you may like it. SR5.LifeStyleOptionRailwayPass_GE: You have a monthly pass to use the light rail or maglev train to travel between two relatively close sprawls. This includes border-crossing fees when relevant (such as when traveling between the various sectors of Denver). This is purchased for two city locations, provided there is a railway connecting them. Examples of possible paired cities include Seattle and San Francisco, San Francisco and Los Angles, Cheyenne and Butte, and St. Louis and Chicago (the O’Hare sub-sprawl, specifically).
SR5.LifeStyleOptionSafehouse_GE: This premise is designated as a safehouse. As such, the character has no control over what Entertainment options are factored into the place, meaning they cannot purchase Entertainment assets for a safehouse, though other assets can be added. Add 4 to the dice pool of anyone trying to track the subject while they reside in a safehouse. The character can freely use the place, but the owner/director has rules that guests must obey while there. The gamemaster decides the house rules (curfew, weapons allowed, clothing restrictions, etc.). This option adds 500 nuyen a month to the cost of a lifestyle.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionSafetyThird_GE: While there is space for a workshop or facility on the premises, it’s not the best of places to work in. In fact, there’s always a risk to your health (for example, no ventilation, wet floor, critters). Reduce the number of 1s needed for a glitch by one (so that if the character would normally need four 1s to glitch, he now only needs three). Characters must have purchased a Shop or Facility along with the Garage or Workshop Asset. Applies to a single asset (Garage or Workshop). This quality can be taken more than once per asset. Add 1 point to the base lifestyle.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionShootingRange_GE: There’s a place you can go where you can shoot guns and not bother the neighbors. Reduce training time with a firearm skill by ten percent.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionSoyProcessingUnit_GE: You have a SOTA set of kitchen devices. SR5.LifeStyleOptionSpecialWorkArea_GE: Applies to a single asset (Garage or Workshop). Can be purchased more than once per lifestyle. The 1,000 nuyen per month additional cost applies each time this is purchased, as does the +2 bonus to the Limit for relevant skill tests performed in the area.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionSportsCourt_GE: This gives the domicile a tennis court, basketball court, driving range, bowling alley, or something like that. The character has a physical place to play at home, saving the need to go out. This reduces training time with an athletics skill by ten percent.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionSwimmingPool_GE: You have every child’s dream—a swimming pool in your home. It may not be a huge pool, but it’s bigger than a bathtub, clean, and deep enough to use for relaxation and exercise.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionThrifty_GE: So what if the shower is lukewarm and the walls are paper thin? You got a great deal on this place. Reduce the points available by 2 and the monthly cost by 1,000 nuyen. Only available for the traveler lifestyle.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionWalkinFreezer_GE: While this chilled room is mainly used for food storage, it can also store things that need to stay cold while six-foot holes are dug as more permanent resting places.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionWorkshopFacility_GE: This is space dedicated to the character’s gear-related work. Power, ventilation, shelving, etc. are there to perform any tasks related to working with an appropriate build and repair skill. Combined with a Shop or Facility, gear/weapons associated with the workshop can be repaired at 1 box of damage per week without additional cost (2 boxes with a Facility).
SR5.LifeStyleOptionWZone_GE: W Zone is sort of like a Z zone, but the W stands for wilderness. This location is way outside any urban area, so the grid is spotty, power is not publicly provided, and unless you have a car, you’re walkin’, as the nearest public transportation is two hours away. Reduce the Neighborhood level by 1 and increase the security response by 1d6 hours. Add 1 point to the base lifestyle.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionYard_GE: You have a piece of outdoor ground that you can consider your own. The lot is roughly fifty to two hundred square meters of empty space, depending on the lifestyle. This could be a backyard to a home, an empty lot, or abandoned parking lot. It’s large enough to park a car, or put up a small kiddy pool, or install a ritual circle. This asset can be purchased more than once to increase the size of the yard.
SR5.LifeStyleOptionZenDenBatCave_GE: Everyone has to have a place to show off their cool stuff, a place where they are surrounded by things that are fun and comfortable. The zen den is a room dedicated to the hobbies of the character. It could be a physical collection of vintage bottles, a trideo set linked to megapulses worth of trid movies, an immersive sports-viewing room, or what-have-you. The zen den provides a +1 dice pool bonus on tests involving relevant Interest Knowledge Skills when the character is at home. The bat cave is similar, though geared more toward legwork. Tools, agent-driven computer simulations, and/or inspirational music provide a helpful atmosphere for the character in solving puzzles. With the purchase of a Kit related to a selected Academic Skill, the bat cave provides a +1 dice pool bonus to tests involving relevant Academic Knowledge Skills made while the character is at home. Separate Kits can be purchased for each Academic Skill, and the bat cave can hold up to three Kits.
SR5.LifestyleSecurity_GE:
Security covers a broad sense of how much a deterrent your place is to unwanted guests and criminal activities other than your own. Those living on the street can only protect what they can hold on to, while people higher up the lifestyle food chain have a physical location that can store and protect their stuff, rather than having to carry it all around with them all the time. Each point into security reduces the risk of theft of the character’s stuff at home. The exact details of when this comes into play are left up to the gamemaster, but one example is a Security Test representing how well the place is watched by security officers, alarms, and other security measures. If anyone attempts a burglary at the character’s domicile while the character is away, roll a dice pool of (Security level x 2) against the Sneaking + Agility of the burglars. If the Security wins the test, security officers have noticed the attempt, or a home alarm has been triggered, or some other event has occurred to indicate that the burglars ran afoul of the security measures without the player having to do a thing. For reference to various aspects of security besides being armed and dangerous, see p. 355, SR5.

The gamemaster should also look at the rare items the character owns compared to the security of the lifestyle. If the item’s Availability is more than twice the Security level, chances are someone/thing will notice the item and want to steal it. The greater the discrepancy, the more likely the item will be targeted.

The gamemaster is encouraged to decide and roleplay out such events, especially if it helps with the adventure/campaign. Alternatively, the gamemaster can abstract the potential for attempted theft with a test using a dice pool equal to the difference between the minimum Security level of a lifestyle required and the actual Security level purchased by the player. For each hit, the player must pay one percent of the monthly cost of the lifestyle to replace stolen goods or repair damaged properly (or pay insurance premiums that help them deal with such things). Nothing exceedingly valuable should go missing in this test. Burglary of a truly valuable item requires the Security Test detailed above.

This is where the middle class lives, along with the commercial places they use and the occasional light industrial facility.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_C:
Response Time: 1D6 x 10 minutes.

The district has seen better days and could use more than just a paint job to bring it up to snuff. You can find low-rent residences, storage facilities, small bodegas, and other similar sites in these zones
SR5.LifeStyleZone_D:
Response Time: 1D6 x 12 minutes.

You can find these zones in the area between industrial and residential districts where the exposure to pollution is a little better than those who live right next to the smoke-churning factories. Or at least, that’s what the residents will tell you. Patrols come through this area, only because it’s inconvenient to go around. D zones can include run-down business district, abandoned warehouses, forgotten tenements, landfills, freeway junctions, old cemeteries, and large parking lots.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_E:
Response Time: 1D6 hours.

These are low-rent/industrial districts mostly filled with SINless squatters and the homeless. Heavy or toxic industrial facilities are included in E Zones. Security providers consider SINless “nonpeople” for the purposes of their work, which means if it’s easier to solve a problem by shooting them, they will.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_Z:
Response Time: 2D6 hours.

This is a lawless area deep in the heart of many barrens. Criminal organizations and gangs can sometimes feel uneasy here. Awakened critters and toxic spirits tend to roam wild. Unless it’s a big incident, most security providers will find routes to avoid going through Z zones. Any type of residence can be found, though it will be in serious disrepair.

SR5.CALENDAR_Description: The Gregorian calendar, leap years included, starting from the world's start year.
SR5.SETTINGS_CalendarStartYear_D: World time zero falls on 1 January of this year, at midnight. Changing the year shifts every date of the world, deadlines included. No effect while a calendar module (Simple Calendar Reborn, Seasons & Stars…) is active.
SR5.CALENDAR_DeadlineIntro: By the world clock ({date}), these deadlines have come. Nothing is rolled or debited until you click.
SR5.CALENDAR_DeadlineRent: {actor}: months of rent paid have run out, {name} ({price} ¥ a month)
SR5.SETTINGS_CalendarRevealDeadlines_D: When ticked, the player also gets the deadlines of their character (withdrawal, rent), without the GM's buttons. Unticked, they stay with the GM, who can show them one at a time from the card.
SR5.WithdrawalResisted: Withdrawal resisted: no craving until the next test
SR5.WithdrawalCraving: Failed: craving, {penalty} dice on tests based on {attributes} until the next fix (SR5 p. 79)
SR5.SETTINGS_WithdrawalModifier_D: The book asks for "the appropriate modifiers for the level of addiction" (SR5 p. 417) without giving them. None: the addiction test pool, nothing more. Craving penalty: −2 Mild, −4 Moderate or Severe, −6 Burnout (values of p. 79).

SR5.CALENDAR_DrugIntro: By the world clock ({date}), these drugs have finished a phase. Nothing changes until you click.
SR5.SETTINGS_CalendarCombatTime_D: Each Combat Turn advances world time by 3 seconds (SR5 p. 51).

SR5.SETTINGS_IndirectDisplayNeutral: Neutral label "External effect", box can be unticked

SR5.SituationalWhen: When? (e.g. against inhaled toxins, at night)
SR5.SituationalUnread: No roll dialog reads this target: the situational effect will never be offered. Pick a skill, a limit, a defense, a resistance, or "Tests".
SR5.SituationalMovementWhen: When? (e.g. running on all fours, hands free)
SR5.SituationalMovementHint: Movement effect: it becomes a box of the Movement block of the sheet, and only counts while it is ticked.
SR5.SituationalHint: Situational effect: tick it only if the situation applies.
SR5.MatrixActionBreakTargetLock_GE: Passive targeting and active targeting with sensors are described on p. 184 of SR5. If you know that you’ve been locked (or suspect it), you can to try to break it. Choose an enemy that has (or you think has) a lock on you, and make the Opposed Test. For every net hit, you reduce the target’s lock on you by one hit. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.
SR5.MatrixActionBruteForce_GE:
You can use this action to mark a target without obtaining the normal permissions you need. This is the action for hackers emphasizing their Attack over their Sleaze, making it related to Hack on the Fly.

If you wish, you may also inflict 1 DV of Matrix damage to the target for every two full net hits, if the target can take Matrix damage, which is resisted with the target’s Device Rating + Firewall.
SR5.MatrixActionCalibration_GE: You can increase the current Initiative Score of a number of personas on whom you have marks by 1 for every 2 hits. The number of personas affected cannot exceed your Data Processing. The Initiative Score then decreases each Combat Turn as normal.
SR5.MatrixActionChangeIcon_GE: You change the target’s icon to one that you have a copy of or have designed yourself. Changing an icon doesn’t change the results of a Matrix Perception action, but might fool personas who don’t take the time to inspect your new look. You can target your own icon, if you like.
SR5.MatrixActionRedefineOwnershipSuccess: Ownership redefined: the device reboots, its owner is ejected, and the AI suffers -2 to all actions for {depth} turn(s)
SR5.MatrixActionEmulateRating: Emulated rating (maximum {max}, added to the Overwatch Score)
SR5.MatrixActionEmulateLegal: Legal action (emulating raises no Overwatch Score)
SR5.MatrixActionCheckOverwatchScore_GE: You find out how close the grid is to converging on you.
SR5.MatrixActionConfusePilot_GE: You send a stream of code to a device with a pilot (usually a drone, but sometimes an autonomous vehicle or gun emplacement) that resembles valid instructions but is in fact gobbledygook. If you succeed, the pilot becomes confused, and makes an immediate Simple Pilot x 2 Test to figure out what it’s going to do next (p. 269, SR5)—the threshold for this test is equal to half of your net hits. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction Rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.
SR5.MatrixActionControlDevice_GE: You perform an action through a device you control (or at least control sufficiently), using your commlink or deck like a remote control or video-game controller.
SR5.MatrixActionCrackFile_GE: You remove the protection from a file, making it readable. This action doesn’t need to be performed on a file that isn’t protected, of course.
SR5.MatrixActionCrashProgram_GE:
You overload part of your target’s memory and scramble one of its running programs.

You need to specify which program you’re trying to crash; you can learn what your target is running either with a Matrix Perception action or by observing the program in action. If you succeed, the program is scrambled: it ends and cannot be restarted until the device it was running on is rebooted.
SR5.MatrixActionDataSpike_GE: You send harmful instructions to a persona or device, causing Matrix damage to the target.
SR5.MatrixActionDenialOfService_GE: A decker or technomancer may target a wirelessly active device or PAN. Make a Computer + Intuition [Data processing] Test opposed by Willpower + Firewall, and apply the number of net hits x 2 as a negative dice pool modifier to all tests made with that device until the beginning of the next Combat Turn. For every mark the decker or technomancer has on an enemy PAN, they may apply this effect to two additional devices slaved to the PAN..
SR5.MatrixActionDetectTargetLock_GE: Passive targeting and active targeting with sensors are described on p. 184 of SR5. An active target lock sends wireless and other signals that hackers and riggers have learned to detect. The RCC, commlink, or deck that you’re using must be wireless-enabled to perform this action. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.
SR5.MatrixActionDisarmDataBomb_GE: You attempt to disarm a Data Bomb that you have detected (usually as the result of a Matrix Perception action). If you score any net hits, the Data Bomb is removed and deleted. If not, the Data Bomb activates, causing its damage and possibly destroying any file to which it was attached (assuming it was set to destroy the file).
SR5.MatrixActionEditFile_GE:
Edit File allows you to create, change, copy, delete, or protect any kind of file. The defender against this test is either the host holding the file or the owner of the file (if it’s not on a host). Each action is enough to alter one detail of a file—a short paragraph of text, a single detail of an image, or two or three seconds of video or audio

If you want to perform a continuous edit, such as removing your teammates from a video feed, you need to perform this action once per Combat Turn for as long as you want to keep the edit going.

If you use this action to copy a file, you are the new file’s owner. If the file you want to copy has protection on it, this action automatically fails. If the file has a Data Bomb, the Data Bomb goes off on you (so try to remember to scan files before you open them).
SR5.MatrixActionEnterOrExitHost_GE: You enter a host that you have a mark on and your icon appears there, or you leave a host you’re already in. There is no test for this action: a host allows anyone to enter if they’ve got a mark, and anyone inside can exit. The host might not be so welcoming once you’re inside, of course, and some IC has the ability to keep you trapped in a host until you can break out.
SR5.MatrixActionEraseMark_GE: You eradicate a mark that has been placed on your persona or on another icon.
SR5.MatrixActionEraseMatrixSignature_GE: You eradicate a Matrix signature that has been left by a Resonance being, such as a technomancer or a sprite.
SR5.MatrixActionFormatDevice_GE:
You rewrite the boot code for the device. The next time it would reboot, it instead shuts down for good, or until its software can be replaced.

A device that has been shut down in this fashion loses all of its wireless modifiers but can still be used as a normal mechanism (a door with a manual handle can be opened, a gun with a trigger can be fired, etc.) and cannot be accessed from the Matrix.
SR5.MatrixActionGarbageInGarbageOut_GE: This allows a decker to “cross the wires” of a single device, confusing its input and output commands. Only a single input can be changed to correspond to a single output—devices can’t be reprogrammed wholesale or made to act in a manner outside of their original design through Garbage In/Garbage Out.
SR5.MatrixActionGridHop_GE:
You hop to another grid—for example, you might jump from the public grid to Seattle’s Emerald City local grid. To do this, you must have access to your destination grid.

If you do not have access, you can use Brute Force or Hack on the Fly to hop to another grid illegally. If you’re inside a host, you need to leave the host before you can hop to another grid.
SR5.MatrixActionHackOnTheFly_GE:
You can use this action to mark a target without getting the normal permissions. This is the action for hackers emphasizing their Sleaze over their Attack, making it an analog to Brute Force.

Additionally, every two full net hits counts as one hit on a Matrix Perception Test, so you can get some info along with your mark.
SR5.MatrixActionHaywire_GE: Target must be a persona not running in VR. Haywire disables all of the target’s PAN-related functions. Physical devices still function, so smartguns can still fire and chemsuits still offer protection, but without wireless or PAN functions. This effect lasts until the target succeeds an extended Computer + Logic [Data Processing] (Hacker’s Net Hits, Simple Action) test with a threshold equal to the net hits from the attacker’s roll; each attempt takes a simple action. The target may simply reset their device and reboot it with a Complex Action; the device will be back online at the end of the following Combat Turn, which takes one minute. Glitching the test to fix the device adds an additional net hit to the attacker’s roll. A critical glitch causes all the devices on the PAN to require an OS reinstall. This takes multiple hours and a connection to a persona-enabled device.
SR5.MatrixActionHide_GE: You’ll probably be spotted by another icon, even if you’re running silent. You can use this action to make a target lose you. If you succeed, the target stops spotting you and needs to perform a new Matrix Perception action against you if it wants to find you again. You can’t hide from an icon that has a mark on you, so you’ll need to clear those before you can try this action.
SR5.MatrixActionIAmTheFirewall_GE:
I Am the Firewall allows the hacker to give a Defense test bonus to all allies with access to an AR feed from the user. The number of bonus dice is equal to the number of hits on a Computer + Intuition [Data Processing] Test. This bonus lasts until the beginning of the hacker’s next Initiative Pass. The hacker can only share their feed with a number of users equal to or less than their Data Processing attribute.

When you take this action as an Interrupt Action, your Initiative Score is reduced by 5.
SR5.MatrixActionIntervene_GE: This allows the hacker to give an immediate defense bonus to the owner of a device slaved to the hacker’s PAN. This action can be taken only if the device making the attack is wirelessly enabled and the hacker is aware of it. When you take this action, your Initiative Score is reduced by 5. Roll your Computer + Intuition [Data Processing], adding the number of hits to your ally’s Defense test. This bonus applies only to the current Defense test—it cannot be carried over to any other Combat Turn or Initiative Pass.
SR5.MatrixActionInterveneEffectNotificat: receives {hits}D on their next Defense test.
SR5.WARN_MatrixSupportNoTarget: Target the allies receiving the effect (or select their token).
SR5.WARN_IAmTheFirewallTooManyTargets: {actor} can only share the AR feed with {max} users (Data Processing): {count} targeted.
SR5.WARN_InterveneSingleTarget: Intervene protects a single ally: target only one.
SR5.MatrixActionInviteMark_GE: If you’re the owner of a device, file, persona, host, or IC program, you can offer other icons the opportunity to put a mark on your device, file, etc. When you make the offer, you choose the number of marks allowed, their duration, and how long the offer stands. The invitee can then mark your icon with a Free Action. You may revoke your offer at any time before the mark is placed, but once another icon has a mark, you need to either use the Erase Mark action or reboot your device to remove it before the duration you chose expires.
SR5.MatrixActionJackOut_GE:
This jacks you out of the Matrix and reboots the device you are using. You suffer dumpshock if you were in VR.

You can only jack out yourself. You can’t dump other people except by beating them into submission through Matrix damage.
SR5.MatrixActionJamSignals_GE:
This action turns the wireless device you are using into a local jammer.

As long as you do not use the device for any further Matrix actions, the device adds any hits you get on the test to the noise rating for all Matrix actions conducted by or targeting any devices within 100 meters.
SR5.MatrixActionJumpIntoRiggedDevice_GE:
You jump into a device that has a rigger adaptation, usually a vehicle or a drone. There’s a list of things you need to have in order to jump into a device: you have to have three marks on the device you want to jump into, you have to be in VR, the device you want to jump into has to have a rigger adaptation, and you have to have a control rig. If you are the device’s owner, or the device’s owner has given you permission to jump into the device, you don’t need to make a test. In the Matrix, the icon of the device you jumped into becomes part of your persona.

If someone else is already jumped into the device, you cannot attempt this action until he or she vacates.
SR5.MatrixActionMasquerade_GE: This action allows a hacker to impersonate a persona on the Matrix. Since persona data is updated in real time, this action requires 2 marks on one target (the persona being impersonated) and 2 marks on a second target (the icon you are trying to fool). For every net hit scored on a Hacking + Intuition [Sleaze] v. Logic + Firewall against the second target, you have convinced them you are target one for one minute. This can be used to impersonate someone online, intercept their calls, use their social media, rummage through their email history, or other creative mischief, but processes like changing device owners or performing major financial actions (like bank transfers) have too many double-checks for Masquerade to work. If the persona you’re impersonating logs off, those marks are immediately lost, and the disguise drops. While masquerading, you are never considered the owner with regard to any of the impersonated persona’s devices.
SR5.MatrixActionMatrixPerception_GE:
This versatile and important action is used both for finding icons in the Matrix and for analyzing Matrix objects. When you use this action to analyze a Matrix object or scan the vicinity for silent-running icons.

For each net hit scored, you can ask for one piece of information about the object—this could be type, a rating, how many marks it has on it, any files it may be carrying, which grid it is using, whether any silent running icons are in the area, or any other pertinent Matrix information. You learn one fact per net hit.
SR5.MatrixActionMatrixSearch_GE: CYou search the Matrix for information about a topic. The time it takes and the threshold of the test depend on the general availability of the information in question and the area being searched, respectively. Any hits above and beyond the threshold can be used to reduce the search time. Divide the base time by the net hits to determine the reduction. If you fail this test, you still spend the full base time looking.
SR5.MatrixActionPopupCybercombat_GE: Target must be a persona not running in VR. If the target has wireless-enabled AR, they are flooded with Matrix spam, taking a penalty to all actions equal to [net hits] until the start of the attacker’s next Combat Turn. If the attacker uses Cybercombat + Logic, the attack also deals Matrix damage equal to net hits.
SR5.MatrixActionPopupHacking_GE: Target must be a persona not running in VR. If the target has wireless-enabled AR, they are flooded with Matrix spam, taking a penalty to all actions equal to [net hits] until the start of the attacker’s next Combat Turn. If the attacker uses Hacking + Logic, they may immediately act as if the net hits on the attack were net hits on a Matrix Perception test, and they gain any relevant information.
SR5.MatrixActionRebootDevice_GE:
The device on which this action is performed shuts down and immediately reboots. The device comes back online at the end of the following Combat Turn. The device ceases electronic functions and disappears from the Matrix until its reboot time is over.

This action only works on devices. It doesn’t work on hosts, living beings (like technomancers, although they can “reboot” themselves, p. 251), or Resonance constructs (like sprites), and the only persona it works on is your own. If you’re the owner of the device you’re rebooting, you don’t have to make a test. You can’t use this action on a device that is link-locked (p. 229).
SR5.MatrixActionSendMessage_GE: You send a text or audio message the length of a short sentence, an image, or a file via the Matrix to a user whose commcode you have. If you’re using the Matrix through a DNI, even if you’re in AR, you can send longer and more complicated messages, about a paragraph worth of text. You can also use this action to open a live feed to one or more recipients, using any digital recording devices you have.
SR5.MatrixActionSetDataBomb_GE:
You set a Data Bomb in a file. When you do, choose the rating of the Data Bomb, up to the net hits on your test. You also need to choose whether or not the Data Bomb will delete the file to which it is attached when activated, and you need to program the passcode required to deactivate it. A file can only have one Data Bomb on it at a time.

The Data Bomb is triggered when someone attempts to read, edit, copy, protect, delete, or put another Data Bomb on the file without using the already-in-place Data Bomb’s passcode. When a Data Bomb goes off, it causes (Rating)D6 Matrix Damage (resisted normally) to the icon that tripped it, deletes the file (if it was set that way), and then is itself deleted. If the passcode is used, the Data Bomb doesn’t activate. Instead, it remains attached to the file, waiting for the next guy.

A Data Bomb can be detected using Matrix Perception. If it’s detected, it can be defused with the Disarm Data Bomb action; a disarmed Data Bomb is deleted. Damn.
SR5.MatrixActionSnoop_GE: This action lets you intercept Matrix traffic sent to and from your target for as long as you have the target marked. You can listen to, view, or read this data live, or you can save it for later playback/viewing if you have something to store it on (your deck will do).
SR5.MatrixActionSpoofCommand_GE: You spoof a device’s owner’s identity, making the device think that your command is a legitimate one from its owner. You need one mark on the icon you are imitating; you do not need a mark on the target. The opposing dice roll is still based on the target, though. This trick only works on devices and agents, not IC, sprites, hosts, personas, or any other icons.
SR5.MatrixActionSquelch_GE: A successful Squelch test prevents the target device from calling or sending messages for a number of minutes equal to the net hits scored.
SR5.MatrixActionSubvertInfrastructure_GE: This action allows a decker or technomancer to slightly alter the operation of multiple physical devices so they respond to the hacker’s commands. If the hacker has at least 1 mark on the host, a successful Electronic Warfare + Intuition [Sleaze] v. Intuition + Firewall Test allows them to control one similar simple device (traffic lights, vending machines, home appliances, desk lamps, etc., at gamemaster discretion) slaved to that host for every net hit. This action cannot be used to make an attack. The hacker can sustain controlling these devices as a Complex Action each Combat Turn.
SR5.MatrixActionSuppressNoise_GE: As described on p. 268, SR5, this action allows riggers to use their RCC to reduce noise between themselves and their vehicles or drones. Reduce noise by the hits on this test, cumulative with any other forms of noise reduction. This effect lasts for the remainder of the current Combat Turn. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.
SR5.MatrixActionSwapTwoPrograms_GE: Swap an active program with a program in memory.
SR5.MatrixActionSwitchInterfaceMode_GE: You switch your perception from AR to VR or vice versa. Switching to VR causes your body to go limp, so don’t do it somewhere dangerous.
SR5.MatrixActionTag_GE:
The hacker may “tag” a number of targets on a single PAN, equal to their net hits, within their line of sight. They can then relay those tags wirelessly to allies. Tagging a target negates up to 2 dice in penalties from Visibility and Light/Glare to any affected ranged attack rolls allies may be making against that target, including blind-fire due to invisibility or shooting through cover. Allies who can see a tag may also take one additional Take Aim Action against that target as a Free Action on each Initiative Pass.

Tags may be sustained by spending a Simple Action to refresh the tags each Combat Turn. When using a PI-Tac, the hacker may add the PITac’s level to the number of targets they may tag. Note: In order for allies to receive this bonus, they must have the ability to see AROs.
SR5.MatrixActionTargetDevice_GE: Pick a wireless-enabled device you’ve spotted on the Matrix. You can target that device and feed targeting data to any pilot program or person with a Sensor rating or smartlink that is slaved to your RCC. For the rest of the Combat Turn, the slaved attackers receive a dice pool bonus equal to your net hits when targeting the device you’re tracking for them. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.
SR5.MatrixActionTraceIcon_GE:
Cette action permet de chercher la localisation physique d’un appareil ou d’un persona dans la Matrice. En cas de réussite, la position réelle de la cible est découverte, et reste connue tant que le personnage a encore au moins une mark sur cette dernière.

Cette action ne fonctionne pas sur les serveurs car ils n’ont généralement aucune présence physique, ni sur les programmes CI car ils n’ont d’existence que sur leur serveur.
SR5.MatrixActionTrackback_GE: You find the physical location of a device or persona in the Matrix. After succeeding with this action, you know the target’s location for as long as you have at least one mark on the target. This doesn’t work on hosts because they generally have no physical location, or IC programs because they are confined to their hosts.
SR5.MatrixActionWatchdog_GE: Target must be a persona or device. If successful, place one mark on the target. The user is now aware of the Matrix actions the target is going to use before they use them, and they may attempt to stop them. A Watchdog mark allows the hacker to use Haywire or Popup as Interrupt Actions (for –10 initiative) or Squelch as an Interrupt Action (for –5 initiative) against the target with the Watchdog mark. This ability lasts as long as the target is marked by the user.
SR5.MatrixSearchInfoTypeHidden: Hidden or Actively Hunted and Erased

SR5.DISEASE_InfectButton: Infect (selected tokens, or list of characters)
SR5.DISEASE_Volunteer: Willing subject (−{n} dice on the first test)
SR5.DISEASE_ReexposedRecovering: {names}: recovering from {name}, the new exposure is not applied (the book says nothing of it). Your call; you may infect again once the recovery is over.
SR5.DISEASE_NoTarget: Tick at least one character to infect.
SR5.DISEASE_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the disease ledger.
SR5.DISEASE_DueFirst: {actor}: incubation of {name} over, first resistance test
SR5.DISEASE_TreatHint: Net hits of the Heal Disease spell (SR5 p. 291), a bonus until the disease ends
SR5.DISEASE_RequestGone: This test was already applied, or the GM asked for another one.
SR5.DISEASE_ZeroReached: An attribute or the Essence is down to 0: death or incapacity as the disease says, for the GM to rule.
SR5.DISEASE_CardPool: The card says: {hits} hits on {pool} dice.
SR5.DISEASE_HitsAbovePool: More hits than dice: the card was edited.
SR5.DISEASE_HitsOnDice: The card's dice show {hits} hits: the card was edited.
SR5.DISEASE_NoDice: The card does not show its dice: type the hits yourself.
SR5.DISEASE_HitsAboveCeiling: The card's dice show {hits} hits, more than the pool and Edge ({pool}): exploding sixes can do it, but the card may have been edited. Type the hits yourself.
SR5.DISEASE_Recovering: Disease beaten: {n} Essence to recover, 1 every 24 hours.
SR5.DISEASE_Damage: Damage for the GM to apply: {value} {type}.
SR5.DISEASE_MemoryLoss: Memory loss: memory test (threshold {threshold}) to use a knowledge or recall the last 12 or 24 hours.
SR5.HardenedArmorHitsOnly: Hardened Armor: only its automatic hits on resistance (Granite skin)
