SR5.HUNGER_Zero: {actor} has no Essence left: it dies on {date} unless it feeds.
SR5.HUNGER_Dead: {actor} did not feed in time: it dies (SR5 p. 403).
SR5.HUNGER_PowerUsed: {actor} used {power}: bring the next Essence loss one week closer?
SR5.INFECTION_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the infection ledger.
SR5.INFECTION_NotZero: Infection can only be tried on a victim whose Essence has fallen to 0 (SR5 p. 401).
SR5.INFECTION_AlreadyComa: This victim is already in the coma of the Infection.
SR5.INFECTION_NoCreature: No creature with the Infection power (and Essence Drain) in the scene or in the world.
SR5.INFECTION_Rule: Only if this creature's Essence Drain brought the victim to 0 (SR5 p. 401). Opposed test: Magic + Charisma of the creature against Body + Willpower of the victim. On a tie, the victim resists (general rule of combat, p. 174).
SR5.INFECTION_Infected: {victim} is infected by {creature} and falls into a coma. Wakes up on {date} as an Infected with 1 point of Essence.
SR5.INFECTION_Offer: The Essence of {victim} has fallen to 0 near a creature with the Infection power. If its Essence Drain emptied the victim: try the Infection?
SR5.INFECTION_Wake: {victim} wakes up from the coma as an Infected (infected by {creature}). The type depends on the original metatype: change the sheet by hand.
SR5.INFECTION_Coma: Coma of the Infection ({creature}): wakes up on {date}
SR5.INFECTION_Woken: Woken from the Infection: set Essence to 1 from the GM's card
SR5.INFECTION_VictimGone: The victim no longer exists (token or actor deleted): it leaves the infection ledger.
SR5.CFD_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the ledger of CFD treatments.
SR5.CFD_DialogIntro: The treatment acts on the Nanite Volume. Several doses given before it takes effect add up: one dose = Rating 1.
SR5.CFD_NanoScrubIVOnly: NanoScrub can only be given intravenously (Dark Terrors p. 87).
SR5.CFD_AerosolTooWeak: As an aerosol the Rating is halved (rounded down): at least 2 doses are needed.
SR5.CFD_OverwritersStarted: {actor} receives Overwriters at Rating {rating}. One roll at the end of each Combat Turn, or "Resolve" on the sheet out of combat.
SR5.CFD_OverwritersRounds: Overwriters against the nanites of {actor} (Rating × 2 [Rating] vs. Volume × 2):
SR5.CFD_Cured: The Nanite Volume of {actor} falls to 0: the CFD infection is eliminated.
SR5.CFD_OverwritersSpent: The Overwriters of {actor} are spent: the treatment fails.
SR5.CFD_ScrubStarted: {actor} receives NanoScrub at Rating {rating}: first effect on {date}, then every hour.
SR5.CFD_ScrubGlitch: Glitch: the NanoScrub destroys the cranial, eye or ear cyberware of {actor} whose base Essence cost is below {n}. To destroy:
SR5.CFD_ScrubGlitchNothing: Glitch: the NanoScrub attacks the implants of {actor} with a base Essence below {n}, but none qualifies.
SR5.CFD_ScrubCritical: Critical glitch: the treatment of {actor} fails and the monad goes psychotic. Unless it already has, the CFD personality overwrites the host on {date}.
SR5.CFD_ScrubTick: NanoScrub, {n} hour(s): {actor} loses {lost} point(s) of Nanite Volume ({volume} left).
SR5.CFD_ScrubCured: NanoScrub: the Nanite Volume of {actor} falls to 0, the CFD infection is removed.
SR5.CFD_ScrubActive: NanoScrub active, Rating {rating}; next effect on {date}
SR5.CFD_Overwritten: The CFD personality has fully overwritten {actor} (Dark Terrors p. 87).
SR5.CFD_ScrubSpent: The NanoScrub of {actor} is spent: the Nanite Volume stays at {volume}, the CFD infection remains.
SR5.CFD_ResolveInCombat: In a combat the Overwriters act at the end of each Combat Turn: "Resolve" is for outside a combat.
SR5.HELP_MonadStrain: Lockdown (p. 206): the device attributes are mental attribute + Nanite Volume, and matrix damage becomes Stun. Original (Dark Terrors p. 88): the Monad is treated as an AI on its nanite swarm (rating and attributes = Nanite Volume), with two monitors, Core and swarm. Dark Terrors p. 91 leaves the choice to the GM.
SR5.HELP_MonadCoreMonitor: The Monad's "source code": 8 + Matrix Entity Concentration / 2. Its damage gives wound modifiers. Matrix damage goes to the swarm; only the GM puts it on the Core, with the button of the damage card (Dark Terrors p. 88).
SR5.MONAD_CoreRule: The matrix damage of an original strain Monad goes to its nanite swarm. The GM may put it on its Core instead, as for an AI (Dark Terrors p. 88, Data Trails p. 161). The suggested number comes from the card: check it.
SR5.MONAD_CoreFullRule: Dark Terrors p. 88: the Monad is dissipated. Its Nanite Volume drops by 1 + the overflow not resisted. It resists the overflow with Willpower + Firewall + Matrix Entity Concentration, as an AI does with its Depth (Data Trails p. 161; DjamZ's ruling, 06/10). At 0 it is destroyed; otherwise it sleeps (10 - Nanite Volume) hours, at least 1.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmFullRule: Dark Terrors p. 88: the Monad is permanently destroyed. The host's current and maximum mental attributes (Logic, Intuition, Charisma, Willpower) drop by Nanite Volume / 4, rounded down. The Nanite Volume drops to 0.
SR5.MONAD_CorePool: Pool: Willpower {willpower} + Firewall {firewall} + Matrix Entity Concentration {cem}.
SR5.MONAD_SurplusFromPlayer: This Core was filled by a player or by hand: the overflow is unknown, type it.
SR5.MONAD_CoreResult: Resistance: {pool} dice, {hits} hits against an overflow of {surplus}. Nanite Volume -{loss}: {before} → {after}.
SR5.MONAD_Sleeps: The personality goes dormant for {hours} h while its source code recompiles.
SR5.MONAD_Destroyed: Nanite Volume at 0: the Monad is permanently destroyed.
SR5.MONAD_Ejected: Any other persona connected to its swarm is ejected and suffers dumpshock where relevant: the GM applies it.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmConfirm: Nanite Volume {volume}: each mental attribute of the host loses {loss} point(s) (never below 1), and the Nanite Volume drops to 0. Apply?
SR5.MONAD_SwarmResult: Swarm bricked (Nanite Volume {volume}): host's mental attributes -{loss}, Nanite Volume at 0.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmReminders: The system keeps no attribute maximum of the actor's own: note the lower maximums. The head case device stays on the sheet, for the GM to remove.
SR5.MONAD_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM resolves the dissipation or the destruction of a Monad.
SR5.MONAD_Gone: This Monad no longer exists or is no longer of the original strain.
SR5.MONAD_Formatted: Swarm formatted: the Monad repairs its boot sector with {actions} Complex Action(s), doing nothing else. If it reboots before, it is destroyed as by a Core overflow (Dark Terrors p. 88).
SR5.MONAD_CoreFromPlayer: This card was written by {user}, not by a GM: the suggested number, like the attack damage it shows, can be forged. Check it against the attack itself.
SR5.MONAD_StrainGMOnly: The CFD strain is the GM's choice (Dark Terrors p. 91): only a GM changes it.
SR5.MONAD_StrainUndone: {user} changed the CFD strain of {name}: put back, it is the GM's choice.
SR5.MONAD_CoreBound: At most {bound} box(es): the Attack of {name} plus its largest matrix action pool, read on its sheet (the most damage its attack can deal, Edge aside).
SR5.MONAD_CoreNoAttacker: Attacker not found: no box can be put on the Core from this card. Change the Core monitor by hand if needed.
SR5.DEFRAG_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM runs a Deactivation.
SR5.DEFRAG_NoCem: First set the Monad's Matrix Entity Concentration (under the Nanite Volume).
SR5.DEFRAG_NoTechnomancer: No character of the world bears the Defragmentation echo.
SR5.DEFRAG_DialogIntro: Expel {target} from its host. It resists with {strength} × 2 dice; {strength} net hits are needed.
SR5.DEFRAG_Connection: A Matrix connection to the target is needed, or a device it can use as a residence (Dark Terrors p. 89).
SR5.DEFRAG_Expelled: Expelled: {target} leaves its host and escapes into the Matrix ({net} net hit{s}, {needed} needed).
SR5.DEFRAG_Failed: The Deactivation fails ({net} net hit{s}, {needed} needed).
SR5.DEFRAG_ExpelledAI: If the AI lived in its home device, it also loses it as its primary residence.
SR5.DEFRAG_PushRefused: (Push the Limit asked, but no Edge is left: refused)
SR5.DEFRAG_InProgress: This request is already being confirmed.
SR5.DEFRAG_NoEcho: This character does not bear the Defragmentation echo.
SR5.DEFRAG_NoTarget: First target the token of the AI or Monad to deactivate.
SR5.DEFRAG_NotTarget: The target is neither an AI nor a Monad: nothing is applied.
SR5.DEFRAG_LaunchIntro: Deactivate {target}. The GM counts the roll again and confirms it before anything is applied.
SR5.DEFRAG_Push: Push the Limit (1 point of Edge, spent when the GM confirms; {n} left)
SR5.DEFRAG_Waiting: Waiting for the GM, who counts again and confirms.
SR5.DEFRAG_ConfirmIntro: {tm} announces {hits} hits against {target} ({test}, announced modifier {modifier}){pushed}. Pool worked out from the sheet, without modifier: {pool} dice {limit}, at most {cap} hits.
SR5.DEFRAG_ConfirmNote: The announced modifier is not taken over: type the one you keep. The hits kept never exceed the ones announced nor what the pool worked out allows. When the limit is pushed, the point of Edge is spent on confirming. The system then rolls the target's resistance.
SR5.DEFRAG_Confirmed: {tm}: {test}{pushed}, {announced} hits announced, pool worked out {pool} dice {limit} → {hits} hits kept by the GM
SR5.DEFRAG_NotOwner: The author of this card does not own this technomancer: nothing is applied.
SR5.DEFRAG_AlreadyDone: This request has already been confirmed.
SR5.DEFRAG_GMRolls: For a GM's technomancer: the system rolls the dice. The player of a technomancer rolls from their own sheet.
SR5.SETTINGS_HungerMonth_T: Essence Loss: length of a lunar month (days)
SR5.SETTINGS_HungerMonth_D: An Infected loses 1 point of stolen Essence per lunar month (SR5 p. 403). The book gives no number of days: 29.5 by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_RevealDiseases_D: When ticked, the player also sees the Power and the number of tests of their character's disease. Unticked, they see only its name and what they feel, and nothing during the incubation.
SR5.PerceptionModSpecificallyLooking: Perceiver is specifically looking/listening for it
SR5.PerceptionModStandsOutInSomeWay: Object/sound stands out in some way
SR5.PORTRAIT_OptimalSize: Optimal picture size is 288 pixels wide by 288 pixels high.
SR5.PreparationFullPotency_D: Hours the preparation keeps its full Potency before losing it (SR5 p. 309): Potency × 2; × 3 with Durable Preparations or for a Godi (Forbidden Arcana p. 39, 71); × 4 for the Islamic alchemist practitioner or with the Sacrifice of blood magic (p. 39, 127). Only the longest counts. Set by the gamemaster.
SR5.PreparationDecayRate_D: After the full time, the preparation loses 1 Potency, then 1 more every hour (SR5 p. 309), or every day with the Fixation metamagic (p. 329). A fovea, a dispersion circle or an alchera hasten it: the gamemaster lowers the Potency by hand. Set by the gamemaster.
SR5.RammingAngleHint: From the rear: difference between the Speeds; on the side: the ramming vehicle's Speed; head-on: both Speeds added. It takes half the damage (rounded up) from the rear or the side, all of it head-on (Rigger 5 p. 179).
SR5.RammingLocomotionHint: Speed is multiplied by locomotion before the table: watercraft ×0.8, ground ×1, rotorcraft ×3, jet ×4 (Rigger 5 p. 184). Vector thrust ×3 and airship ×1 are a table ruling, the book is silent. Rounded to the nearest, at least 1 when the vehicle moves.
SR5.RammingGaitHint: Against a pedestrian or an object: the target must be within the vehicle's walking or running range, -3 dice when running (SR5 p. 203). The gait fills in the relative speed from the vehicle's Speed; the GM may correct it.
SR5.RammingRelativeSpeedHint: Relative speed in meters per turn, for the Collision Damage table (SR5 p. 203-204).
SR5.RangeWithEnvironment_D: Range is an environmental modifier (SR5 p. 176): only the worst condition counts, one row further when several are equally severe. This line gives what range adds to the Environment line.
SR5.HELP_OrichalcumEditMsg: Left click: −1, right click: +1. Orichalcum replaces any reagent; its uses stay in the GM's hands (Street Grimoire p. 209-210, Forbidden Arcana p. 184).
SR5.ReagentForeignHint: Another tradition's reagents work at only half their Power (SR5 p. 320).
SR5.ReagentHarvestZoneHint: An hour of astral perception, then Alchemy + Magic [Mental] (SR5 p. 320). Overharvested area: Forbidden Arcana p. 181.
SR5.ReagentHarvestZone_tradition: Suited to my tradition (1 drachm / 2 hits)
SR5.SETTINGS_ReagentSystem_D: Core rulebook: a single stock of drachms. Shadow Spells: raw, refined, radical reagents and orichalcum, refining. Forbidden Arcana: the same, each tier also giving a limit and Drain bonus.
SR5.WARN_BindingReagents: Binding needs {reagents} drachms of reagents (SR5 p. 304).
SR5.RitualCircleLeader: Leader: {name}. Participants announce themselves before the sealing.
SR5.RitualCircleSealed: The leader seals the ritual: no one can join anymore.
SR5.RitualAssistNoSkill: Without the Ritual Spellcasting skill, no die to add; the Drain is still taken.
SR5.RitualAssistOtherTradition: Tradition different from the leader's: -2 dice.
SR5.RitualAssistGlitch: Glitch: this participant does not raise the leader's limit.
SR5.RitualAssistCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: no participant raises the leader's limit.

SR5.BGPhenomenonHint: Aetherology p. 33-35: fills the rating and alignment, which you may then change within the book's range.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_astralRift: Astral rift (AETH p. 33-34): mundanes may project; uninitiated pass without the Dweller on the Threshold. A mundane whose body leaves the rift, or whose rift closes, fades after [Essence] hours.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_astralShallows: Astral shallows (AETH p. 34): switching to astral perception is a Free Action; mundanes see the astral without touching it.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theMist: The Mist (AETH p. 34), Force 3 to 10: noise + Force (applied); Force as a penalty to ranged attacks and Perception; Confusion (Magic = Force x 2); Movement; +2 Composure threshold, one test per hour; -1 to spirits' tests, which try to flee; rifts from 6.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_daoineannDraoidheil: Daoineann Draoidheil (AETH p. 34), Force 8 to 12, druidic: fixed mana storm; every spell and triggered preparation scatters randomly.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_fovea: Fovea (AETH p. 34-35), ebb 7 to 12: preparations lose 1 Potency every 30 min (6 h if anchored); the fovea loses 1 Force every 2 h and fades below 4.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_mayaCloud: Maya Cloud (AETH p. 35), Force 14 to 16: noise + Force (applied); Force as a penalty to Perception in and through the cloud.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theVeil: The Veil (AETH p. 35), Force 12 to 14: sustains a Chaotic World spell at its Force; crossing without electronic navigation exits elsewhere.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theVoid: The Void (AETH p. 35), ebb 13 to 20: reagents are drained; a focus left more than [Force] hours is destroyed.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_manaStorm: Mana storm (AETH p. 34): see Street Grimoire p. 36; enter its Force.

SR5.ManaShiftApply_ebb: Apply Mana Ebb to the scene (−1, {hours} h)

SR5.ManaShiftApplied_ebb: Mana Ebb: the background count of "{scene}" drops by 1 for {hours} h.
SR5.ManaShiftFails_flux: Mana Flux fails: it only succeeds on a negative background count (here {count}). The Drain is still resisted (Shadow Spells p. 25).
SR5.ManaShiftFails_ebb: Mana Ebb fails: it only succeeds on a positive background count (here {count}). The Drain is still resisted (Shadow Spells p. 25).

SR5.ManaShiftNoScene: No scene to apply the ritual to.

SR5.ManaShiftAlreadyApplied: This ritual card has already been applied.
SR5.ManaShiftConfirm: Apply {name} (Force {force}) to the scene {scene}: background count shifted by 1 for {hours} hours?
SR5.ManaShiftHint: Shadow Spells p. 25: each one moves the count by 1 toward 0 for [Force] hours of game time, never past 0. A ritual that has run out goes away when game time passes.
SR5.GreyManaSustainedSpell: Grey mana (Better Than Bad p. 140): {spell} is sustained with 1 less Force and 1 less hit.
SR5.ToxinEffectManasphereCut_GE: Better Than Bad p. 141: no magic of any kind (Magic brought to 0: no spell, adept powers off) for [12 − (Body or Magic, the higher)] hours, at least 1 hour. A dual-natured being also takes −4 dice to every action. Over 24 hours of continuous exposure: mutations, then death.
SR5.ToxinBlightSpecial: Only affects the Awakened and dual-natured beings.
SR5.ToxinBlightDmsoSpecial: An Awakened resists with their Drain resistance instead of toxin resistance, and the damage is Stun Drain. A spirit exposed loses its Immunity to Normal Weapons against this damage.

SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumBaseWeapons_D: Compendium searched for the base weapons given to new actors (spirit natural attacks, unarmed strike...). Items are recognized by their system effects (baseOwnItem), not by their name.
SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumCreaturePowers_D: Compendium searched for the base and optional powers of spirits. Items are recognized by their system effects (spiritPower), not by their name. On automatic, a power missing from sr5-compendiums is looked for in the Megapack when it is active.
SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumSpritePowers_D: Compendium searched for the base and optional powers of sprites. Items are recognized by their system effects (baseOwnItem, spritePower), not by their name.
SR5.SETTINGS_CyberEyesReplaceNaturalVisi: A character wearing cybereyes loses the vision its metatype gave it, unless it bought that vision again as an enhancement: this is the rule (SR5 p. 96). Uncheck it only if your table chooses to keep both.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevLogActive_D: Display Shadowrun 5 system development messages in the browser/app console.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevLogLevel_D: Filtering level of displayed development messages.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevicelessAILogicDefense_D: An AI outside any device defends against Matrix actions with its Willpower or Intuition alone, depending on the action (Data Trails p. 157), with no Matrix attribute. The book does not say which one replaces Logic when the defense calls for it: this setting picks it. Defenses using Willpower or Intuition keep them. The same attribute resists Matrix damage, for which the book gives no pool without a device or Firewall (Data Trails p. 157 and 161).
SR5.SETTINGS_DevicelessAILogicDefense_T: AI outside a device: attribute replacing Logic in defense and resistance
SR5.SETTINGS_HomunculusMaterialArmor_D: The book (SR5 p. 301) gives a homunculus the Structure of its material as Body, and no Armor. Checked, it also gets the Armor of that material (Barrier Ratings table, SR5 p. 198).
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_D: What bounds an augmented physical or mental attribute (cyberware, bioware, magic). The book: +4 at most over the natural rating (SR5 p. 96). The excess is removed, and the attribute's tooltip shows the real and the kept values. Magic, Resonance and Edge are not concerned.
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_bonus: +4 at most over the natural rating (book, SR5 p. 96)
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_augmentedMa: Augmented maximum only: metatype maximum + 4 (SR5 p. 68, 290, 312)
SR5.AugmentationCapReason_boost: spell or adept power bounded by the augmented maximum, SR5 p. 290 and 312
SR5.AugmentationCapUnknownMetatype: Cap: metatype unknown to the table (SR5 p. 68), no cap applied
SR5.SETTINGS_FreeReload_T: Reload without spending an action (house rule)
SR5.SETTINGS_FreeReload_D: The book has reloading cost actions (SR5 p. 167 and table p. 169). Checked, reloading in combat costs no action when the right rounds are in the inventory, and a full refill becomes possible. Ejecting a clip alone keeps its cost.
SR5.SETTINGS_MentorMask_T: Mask of the mentor (Forbidden Arcana p. 176)
SR5.SETTINGS_MentorMask_D: Optional rule: a magician reduces all their Drain by 1 (never below 2), an adept gains 1 Power Point.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritLeash_D: Optional rule: a tight leash counts as a sustained spell (−2), and a spirit scoring 6 − (Force / 2) hits or more offers the gamemaster a leash test.
SR5.SpiritElemental_D: Elemental trait (Forbidden Arcana p. 175): mental attributes lowered by Force / 2 (minimum 1), one more service when summoned or bound, never tests the leash.
SR5.SpiritWild_D: Wild spirit (Forbidden Arcana p. 170-172): cannot be summoned; banished against Force × 2, net hits adding up to Force × 2.
SR5.SpiritDomain_D: Domain trait (Forbidden Arcana p. 172): Magic × 2 for Accident, Guard and Search.
SR5.SpiritMagicPact_D: Magic pact of a free spirit (Street Grimoire p. 133): the spirit may spend the Edge of the character who summoned it. Without it, a spirit never spends its summoner's Edge (SR5 p. 58).
SR5.AstralReputationAdjustment_D: Added to the reputation from the index: +6 for the hermetic elementalist (Forbidden Arcana p. 175), −1 per conjuring geas, atonement (Street Grimoire p. 207).
SR5.HermeticElementalist_D: Forbidden Arcana p. 175: his air, earth, fire and water spirits get the Elemental trait. Remember the +6 adjustment.

SR5.INFO_WildSpiritDissipated: {name} is dissipated. Until the end of the banisher's next action, a magician may try to bind it (Forbidden Arcana p. 172).

SR5.LeashBroken: No service left: the spirit tries to return to its metaplane on its next turn; if mistreated, or against an Astral Reputation of 4 or more, it attacks its former controller (Forbidden Arcana p. 176).

SR5.MentorExtraWarning: A character follows a single mentor (SR5 p. 76): only the first one applies.
SR5.LinkedMentorHint: This character's Mentor Spirit item that carries the bonuses, the drawback and the Mask (SR5 p. 76). A mentor spirit of the character can also be dropped here.

SR5.MentorWarning_mysticPath: {mentor}: mystic adept, choose the mentor's path (SR5 p. 324)

Unchecked: core rulebook.

SR5.BB_BleedRow: is bleeding: +1 Physical box (Bullets & Bandages p. 14)

SR5.BB_StabilizeConfirmNoReduction: Stabilize {name}? The wound stops getting worse.

Success: +2 dice on the next stabilization or treatment test, +1 on a glitch, -2 on a critical glitch.
SR5.BB_DiagnoseResult: Diagnosis of {name}: {bonus} dice on the next care.
SR5.BB_MedkitEmpty: The medkit has no supplies left: -3 penalty (Bullets & Bandages p. 18).

SR5.BB_ImprovisedHits_D: Bullets & Bandages p. 18: a Complex Action of First Aid + Intuition; each hit takes 1 off the -3 penalty (3 at most). First aid then takes one and a half times as long.
SR5.BB_DiagnoseButton: Diagnosis: {hits} hits (threshold set by the GM)

SR5.SETTINGS_LowLightGreenTint_D: Night-vision goggles green tint on what a token using low-light vision sees. A visual convention, not a rule: the book only says low-light vision lets one see normally in dim light (SR5 p. 447). Off, the token sees in natural colours. The tint only shows while a single token is selected (a Foundry limit).

SR5.SpriteCompanionDescription: Companion sprites are always by your side, right when you need them. They exist to protect and serve.
SR5.SpriteCourierDescription: Courier sprites are great at delivering messages securely and are pretty good trackers.
SR5.SpriteCrackDescription: If you need a sprite for a quiet run that stays under the radar, the Crack sprite has what you need.
SR5.SpriteDataDescription: Data sprites are masters of finding and manipulating data. They make great librarians, searchbots, and trivia contest ringers.
SR5.SpriteFaultDescription: The Fault sprite is the one you want to have your back in a fight. Cold as IC and twice as tenacious, they’ll shred your enemies in the blink of an icon.
SR5.SpriteGeneralistDescription: Not particularly good at any one thing, but also not bad. They are what you make of them.
SR5.SpriteMachineDescription: Of all the sprites, the Machine sprite is the most likely to interact with the physical world, although that would happen through a device. They’re experts at all sorts of electronics.
SR5.STATUSES_BleedOut_GE: Target suffers 1P DV, unresisted, for every Action they perform that is not First Aid until a successful Logic + First Aid [Mental] (4) Test is made) or a Heal spell is cast on them and removes at least 1 box of damage).
SR5.STATUSES_Blinded_GE: One eye: –4 all actions involving sight; Two eyes: –8 on all actions, no vision-based Perception tests allowed for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.
SR5.STATUSES_BrokenGrip_GE: Target is unable to maintain their grip on anything in their hand, suffers a –1 dice pool penalty per injured arm for all Subduing or Clinching attacks, and drops any item in their hand for a number of Combat Turns equal to the DV of the attack.
SR5.STATUSES_Buckled_AGE: Target makes Body ({DV}) Test or else they hit the ground and stay there for ({DV})-hits Combat Turns.
SR5.STATUSES_Buckled_GE: Target makes Body (DV) Test or else they hit the ground and stay there for (DV)-hits Combat Turns.
SR5.STATUSES_Deafened_GE: One ear: –2 all actions involving hearing; Two ears: –4 on all actions, no hearing-based Perception tests allowed for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.
SR5.STATUSES_DirtyTrick_GE: This shot does no damage, but the opponent receives a -{value} penalty on next action. Pulling a Dirty Trick shot with different types of ammo can enhance the effect.
SR5.STATUSES_Entanglement_GE: The character can use a rope or whip-like weapon to entangle her opponents instead of outright killing them. In an Armed Combat Attack using an Exotic Melee Weapon Skill, the character can use net hits from the attack to reduce the opponent’s Agility for that Action Phase instead of dealing damage from the weapon. If the attack generated any net hits at all, the opponent cannot move any further away from the character than the range of the weapon. If the opponent’s Agility is reduced to 0, the opponent can do no other action than attempt to break free. Like a subdual or clinch, the opponent will have to break free of the entanglement in order restore his agility attribute. If they want to get away, the opponent can attempt an Escape Artist + Agility [Physical] Test as a Complex Action with a threshold of the number of successes used to reduce his Agility. If successful, the opponent is free and no longer suffers from the Agility penalty. Weapons that can be used with this called shot include: chain whip, leather whip, manrike, kusarigama, rope dart, and lariat. Note that use of this action requires Martial Art training
SR5.STATUSES_Fatigued_GE: Target makes a secondary Damage Resistance Test using Body only against Stun damage equal to half the DV of the original attack.
SR5.STATUSES_Flared_GE: –8 penalty on any action taken in the character’s next Action Phase, no vision-based Perception tests allowed for thirty seconds (ten Combat Rounds).
SR5.STATUSES_FuelTankBattery_GE: Disables vehicle. Causes fuel leak or battery leak.
SR5.STATUSES_Knockdown_AGE: Target must make a Strength + Agility ({DV+3}}) Test or fall prone.
SR5.STATUSES_Knockdown_GE: Target must make a Strength + Agility (DV+3) Test or fall prone.
SR5.STATUSES_Nauseous_GE: Target makes a Body + Willpower (4) roll; each hit less than the required 4 causes the target to double over and begin vomiting for one Combat Turn. Vomiting targets suffer a –4 dice pool penalty to all actions.
SR5.STATUSES_OneArmBandit_GE: Target’s arm is ineffective and they are unable to perform any actions with that limb for a number of Combat Turns equal to the DV of the attack; they also suffer a –6 dice pool penalty until that arm is healed), Weak Side (target suffers a –2 dice penalty on all melee Defense tests while their arm is ineffective/
SR5.STATUSES_OnPinsAndNeedles_GE: Rough Terrain (Requires 1 shot per square meter, 1/2 Movement through terrain; if the target is barefoot they suffer 3P resisted with Body)
SR5.STATUSES_Pin_GE: With an appropriate ranged weapon, the character can pin an opponent to the floor, the ground, or a wall. On a successful attack with the weapon, if the DV exceeds the Armor Rating of the target’s clothing (meaning augmentations like dermal plating would not be taken into account), then the flesh and clothing of the opponent are pinned to that object. Net hits determine how securely the opponent is pinned. While the opponent is pinned, he suffers a –2 penalty to all Defense Tests. To break free of a pin, the character can make a Body + Strength [Physical] Test as a Simple Action with a threshold of the net hits of the pin. The character can also rip himself free as a Free Action, but takes 1 box of unresisted physical damage for each net hit on the Pin Called Shot. Both the Simple and Free Action can be attempted in the same Action Phase. If the Simple Action fails, the difference between the hits rolled and the threshold are added to the Physical Damage the character takes when attempting to break free. Note that use of this action requires Martial Art training.
SR5.STATUSES_Shaked_GE: The target suffers -1 penalty for being shaken.
SR5.STATUSES_SlowDeath_GE: Physical Damage attacks only, must be with piercing weapon; injuries cause the target to bleed internally, suffering unresisted 2S DV every minute until a Medicine + Logic [Mental] (16, 1 minute) Extended Test, First Aid + Logic [Mental] (16, 1 minute) Extended Test is successful, or a Heal spell is cast on them and removes at least 1 box of damage.
SR5.STATUSES_Slowed_GE: Target’s Movement, both Walk and Run rate, is halved and no Sprint Tests are allowed.
SR5.STATUSES_Stunned_GE: Body + Willpower Test to resist or target receives a penalty to Initiative Score. Threshold and penaly depend on location.
SR5.STATUSES_TrickShot_GE: Net hits on this Called Shot add to the shooter’s dice pool on Intimidation Tests against the target.
SR5.STATUSES_UnableToSpeak_GE: The target loses the ability to form understandable speech. They can mutter, gesture, groan, and drool, but everything they try to speak comes out as gibberish. This lasts for 1 hour x DV of the shot.
SR5.STATUSES_WeakSide_GE: The target suffers a –1 dice pool penalty on all melee Defense tests while they suffer from the effects of Broken Grip.
SR5.STATUSES_Winded_GE: Target is unable to perform Complex Actions for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.

When checked, each character's "Wired by DNI" box decides. When unchecked (default), switching the wireless is a free action for everyone. Same rule for a firearm with its wireless on: ejecting the clip, changing the firing mode or the choke are free with a DNI (p. 427 and 435).
SR5.HELP_DNIWiredMsg: The character commands their devices through a direct neural interface: switching their wireless is a free action (SR5 p. 165), a simple action otherwise (p. 167). SR5.ToxinEffectAgony_GE: The character is broken by an unbearable pain that is difficult to describe. If the residual Power of the toxin exceeds the character's Willpower, he or she can no longer speak coherently or move faster than by crawling slowly.
SR5.ToxinEffectArcaneInhibitor_GE: Venom with this quality temporarily reduces the victim’s Magic by the Power of the venom. If the Power is greater than the victim’s Magic Rating, they cannot use Magic until the power of the venom is reduced. As the Power is reduced, Magic comes back normally.
SR5.ToxinEffectDisorientation_GE: Disorientation causes the victim a –2 dice pool modifier to all actions for ten minutes, due to confusion and disorientation.
SR5.ToxinEffectNausea_GE: Nausea is a catch-all term; it includes pain, panic, vomiting, and double vision. If the Power of an attack after the Toxin Resistance Test exceeds the target’s Willpower, he is incapacitated (unable to take any actions) with vomiting and dizziness for 3 Combat Turns. Whether or not a character is incapacitated, Nausea doubles all of a character’s wound modifiers for ten minutes. A nauseated character with 3 boxes of damage (a –1 wound modifier), for example, suffers –2 dice on all tests instead.
SR5.ToxinEffectParalysis_GE: Paralysis renders the victim unable to move by blocking the body’s neuromuscular signals. If the Power of an attack after the Toxin Resistance Test exceeds the target’s Reaction, the target is paralyzed and unable to take physical actions for 1 hour. Even if the target is not paralyzed, he suffers a –2 dice pool modifier for the next hour.

SR5.AddictionBurnoutEither: Body or Willpower, by a coin toss (tie, SR5 p. 416)
SR5.AddictionBurnoutLoss: {name} fails an addiction test ({drug}) at Burnout: 1 point of {attribute} is lost for good, and 1 point of its maximum (SR5 p. 416). At 0, coma: both monitors filled, plus 1 box of physical overflow. To apply by hand.
SR5.AddictionTestReminder: {drug}: an addiction test will be due after {weeks} weeks of use (11 − rating {rating}), threshold {threshold}. Roll it from the Addictions list, Qualities tab (SR5 p. 415).
SR5.WARN_AddictionNotFound: This addiction is no longer on the sheet.
SR5.HELP_AddictionTestMsg: Body + Willpower when physiological, Logic + Willpower when psychological, both tests when both: one failure is enough (SR5 p. 415). The threshold is the Addiction Threshold.
SR5.HELP_AddictionLevelMsg: The Addiction quality (SR5 p. 79-80): Mild, Moderate, Severe, Burnout. Each failed test raises it one level.
SR5.MilkBrickUsed: {name}: the brick of milk removes {removed} (No Future p. 154).
SR5.MilkBrickNothing: {name}: the brick of milk is drunk but removes nothing: no Nausea or Disorientation it soothes (No Future p. 154).
SR5.WARN_MilkBrickNotOwner: You do not own {name}: the brick of milk is not used. Ask the gamemaster.
SR5.AddictionResistanceNote: Applies to every addiction test. Drug Tolerant (Chrome Flesh p. 58) only covers natural and synthetic drugs.
SR5.FACTION_OnlyGM: Only the active gamemaster edits factions.
SR5.FACTION_MenuHint: Faction Reputation (Cutting Aces p. 156): factions, members, movements, spending and journal. Gamemaster only.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_MenuHint: Actors and contacts imported before the Negotiation fix lost it (0). The window lists those whose source compendium gives more, and the gamemaster ticks what applies; each correction is applied once per sheet.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_Intro: These sheets read a Negotiation of 0 while their source compendium gives one. A 0 set on purpose looks the same as a lost one: tick only what you want back. A sheet already restored is not offered again; what is left unticked stays.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_OnlyActiveGM: Only the active gamemaster can apply the repair.
SR5.FACTION_Hint: Faction Reputation (Cutting Aces p. 156-160). Pending movements apply at the end of the mission, with Karma. The gamemaster always keeps the last word on NPC attitude.
SR5.FACTION_DeleteConfirm: Delete the faction {name} and its whole journal?
SR5.FACTION_Pending: Pending (applied at the end of the mission)
SR5.FACTION_ApplyPending: End of mission: apply pending movements
SR5.FACTION_PickFactionActor: Choose a faction and at least one character.
SR5.FACTION_NotEnough: Not enough reputation: {score} for a cost of {cost} (never below zero, p. 159).
SR5.FACTION_ContactNotInFaction: This contact must belong to this character and to this faction.
SR5.FACTION_OnceAMonth: This contact's Influence was already raised this month (once a month, p. 159). Go on anyway?
SR5.IllusionNotPierced: {observer} does not see through the illusion ({spell}).
SR5.TacnetHint: At most Device Rating × 1.5 members, drones included (Run & Gun p. 119). The bearer asks, the GM confirms.
SR5.TacnetInactive: The network gives nothing until the item is active with its wireless on.
SR5.TacnetRosterHint: The roster is kept by the GM. Each member picks his combat mode skill (levels II and III).
SR5.TacnetFull: PI-Tac “{network}” is full ({max} members): {member} does not join.
SR5.TacnetRefused: The GM refuses the change of {member} in PI-Tac “{network}”.
SR5.TacnetTrimmed: The rating of “{network}” now allows {max} member(s) only: {members} leave(s) the network.
SR5.IllusionCardRejected: Illusion card ignored ({spell}, sent by {user}): it does not come from the character's owner, or its dice do not fit his pool.
SR5.IllusionConfirm: {user}: {caster} casts {spell} on {subject}. Threshold for whoever resists: {threshold}. Record it?
SR5.IllusionConfirmMismatch: The card claims {claimed} hits, its dice show {hits}: {hits} is kept.
SR5.IllusionConfirmTarget: This token was not targeted by the card's author when the roll was made.
